Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT: An open AI agent platform that automatically breaks a goal down into tasks. It can choose tools, run steps, and organize results on its own, so you can focus on what you want done without building the whole toolchain from scratch. You only need to give it a goal, and the execution can be self-hosted.
langgenius/dify: A platform for building agent workflows and RAG applications. You can connect multiple models, knowledge bases, and tools, arrange them in a visual flow, then put the result in the cloud or host it yourself as an application that can chat and carry out tasks. Finished applications can be opened directly by other people through a chat interface.
langflow-ai/langflow: Build and deploy AI agents and workflows with visual flows. Each node can be a model, a prompt, a tool, or a data source, and drawing connections forms a flow you can try and run right away. After a flow is saved, you can change the nodes without starting over.
langchain-ai/langchain: An engineering platform for developing agents, assembling models, tools, memory, and flows into reusable applications. It suits people who want to control each step in code, rather than relying on one large prompt, and who want to connect their own data and systems. It suits engineers who need to connect databases, APIs, and their own internal systems.
browser-use/browser-use: A Python library that lets an AI agent control a browser. It can open pages, click buttons, fill forms, and extract data on its own, turning browsing into actions an agent can complete without you writing selectors step by step. Steps such as logging into an admin backend and moving data across pages can be handed to it to try.
google-gemini/gemini-cli: An open-source agent that brings Gemini into the terminal. You can assign development work from the command line and have it read the project, suggest changes, and run commands without leaving the terminal you already use. After the edits, they can stay in the original repo, so you do not have to switch to another editor.
infiniflow/ragflow: An open-source engine that combines retrieval-augmented generation with agents. It splits documents, builds indexes, and retrieves sourced context when answering, so the large model does not have to answer from its own memory alone. When an answer is wrong, you can check it against the cited passages instead of looking only at the final sentence.
OpenHands/OpenHands: An agent that uses AI for software development. You can hand it a development task, and it will edit code, run commands, read test results, and keep fixing based on failures, rather than only emitting a suggested snippet. A failed test stays in the same round so it can keep editing until the tests pass.
bytedance/deer-flow: A long-horizon agent framework for research, coding, and creative work. Complex tasks are split and handed to sandboxes, memory, and sub-agents to handle separately, so one conversation does not have to remember every step from the start. Research, coding, and creative work can be split into different subtasks and run together.
ruvnet/ruflo: An agent harness for coordinating multiple agents, automated workflows, and conversational systems with memory. The focus is putting roles, tools, and state in the same execution environment so they can finish longer tasks together. State does not disappear when a new conversation starts, which is what longer workflows need.
FoundationAgents/MetaGPT: A multi-agent framework that organizes product, design, and engineering roles into a software team. You describe requirements in natural language, and they divide the work by role to produce designs and code, rather than having one chatbot do everything at once. Outputs are filed by role, so you can review only the design or only the code.
cline/cline: A coding agent that can write code on its own, with an IDE extension, an SDK, and a command-line interface. It can read a project, edit files, and run commands, which suits people who want to assign development work directly inside the editor. The same instructions can be reused in the editor or on the command line.
openinterpreter/openinterpreter: A coding agent aimed at open-source models that can write code and run commands on the local machine. You describe what you want in natural language, and it generates and runs programs on your machine, with files and the environment staying local. Generated programs run locally, and result files stay on your computer.
mem0ai/mem0: A memory layer for AI agents. Facts worth remembering in a conversation are extracted and stored, then retrieved in later conversations, so the agent does not treat you as a first meeting every time. When a new session starts, it can look up old facts so the user does not have to say them again.
Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm: A self-hostable, local-first workspace. Documents, conversations, and agents stay on your own machine or your own server, which suits people who want question answering over private data without handing the files over. Private files can stay only on your own server while you still ask questions about them.
microsoft/autogen: Microsoft's agent programming framework for orchestrating multiple AIs that can converse and use tools. You can define each agent's role and the functions it can call, then let them take turns discussing until the task is done. It suits workflows where several specialized roles review one another before a result is delivered.
crewAIInc/crewAI: Forms autonomous agents in different roles into a team that completes more complex tasks together. Each member has its own goal and tools, and the flow decides who goes first and who continues, rather than one agent doing everything. What you change is the division of roles, not one prompt that keeps getting longer.
aaif-goose/goose: An extensible AI agent that does more than suggest code: it can also install, run, edit, and test. It operates the development environment on the local machine according to your instructions, which suits people who want a terminal assistant that can actually do the work. Installing dependencies and running tests are things it does itself, not only producing a diff.
FlowiseAI/Flowise: Build AI agents and language-model flows by drag and drop. Nodes can connect models, memory, and tools, which suits people who want to try a flow graphically first. The repository is archived, but it is still a common visual starting point. The repository is archived, and it is now better suited as a teaching reference and a reference for older flows.
CherryHQ/cherry-studio: A desktop AI workspace that puts chat, autonomous agents, and a large set of assistants in one program. You can connect different model providers and use a local interface to manage conversations, tools, and common workflows. When you switch model providers, the conversations and the assistant list still stay on the local machine.
run-llama/llama_index: A document processing and retrieval platform for connecting data to AI applications that can query and take action. It loads documents, builds indexes, and retrieves, then hands the result to a model to answer or to an agent to continue. Process the documents first, then decide whether to do question answering or hand the work to an agent.
HKUDS/nanobot: A lightweight, self-hostable personal agent framework. It includes a web interface, tools, memory, and multi-agent workflows, which suits people who want to run a small assistant on their own machine without first deploying a full platform. If you want a small-scale assistant first, you do not have to deploy a large platform at the start.
zhayujie/CowAgent: An open-source personal AI assistant that can plan tasks and use tools and skills. It remembers conversations and knowledge, so later tasks can refer to what it learned before instead of starting from an empty context every time. Skills and knowledge accumulate, so you repeat the same instructions less often.
langchain-ai/langgraph: Orchestrate reliable agent flows with a graph. Nodes and edges can express branches, loops, and human confirmation, which suits tasks whose steps loop back, or that take a long time to finish, rather than a straight line of calls. Requiring a person to press confirm, or going back to try again after a failure, can both be drawn as a graph.
agno-agi/agno: A self-improving agent platform for building and running AI agents. You can define tools and knowledge so the agent accumulates experience after a run and takes fewer detours the next time it handles similar work. Once a similar job has been done, the next time it can follow the earlier approach.
666ghj/BettaFish: A multi-agent public-opinion analysis assistant, implemented from scratch. Several roles divide the work of collecting public discussion, organizing a timeline, and reconstructing the event, helping you judge how a topic spread rather than only returning a pile of links. It suits tracking how one public event developed, rather than writing a general chatbot.
stanfordnlp/dspy: Compose language models in code instead of handwritten prompts. You split a task into modules, and the framework optimizes the prompt for each step, which suits people who want to tune a flow systematically rather than trying prompts sentence by sentence. When the task changes, you change the modules instead of manually trying a new prompt each time.
continuedev/continue: An open-source coding agent that can read and write code and finish development tasks inside the editor. It sees the current project context and edits, explains, and runs according to your instructions, without you pasting the whole repository into a chat window. Instructions are aimed at the files you have open, which reduces pasting the wrong context.
OpenBMB/ChatDev: Uses multiple language-model agents to play a development team and collaborate on software design and implementation. Roles such as product, coding, and testing take turns handing off work, moving one requirement toward code you can read, rather than generating it all at once. One requirement runs through the whole small team before you see readable code.
openai/openai-agents-python: OpenAI's lightweight Python framework for orchestrating multi-agent workflows. You can define handoffs, tools, and guardrails so several agents divide the work, which suits people who want to write agents directly against the official interface. If you want to follow OpenAI's current agent interface, this is closer to the official one than older tutorial frameworks.
assafelovic/gpt-researcher: An autonomous research agent that can gather material on a topic and write a sourced research report. It plans what to look up, reads the results, and synthesizes them, rather than answering only from a few passages you pasted in. You only need to give it a topic, without first finding ten papers yourself and pasting them in.
huggingface/smolagents: Hugging Face's compact agent library. Agents mainly think and act by writing code, turning a step-by-step plan into an executable program, which suits people who want little abstraction and direct control over tool calls. When a step goes wrong, you can look back at the program it wrote instead of a vague piece of reasoning.
mastra-ai/mastra: A framework for building AI applications and agents in TypeScript. Workflows, tools, and model calls are organized in code, so they fit into an existing web or server project without standing up a separate Python service. A service that already uses TypeScript can connect directly, without opening a separate Python service.
microsoft/semantic-kernel: Microsoft's SDK for connecting large language models, plugins, and planning into an application. You define skills in code, then let the model decide when to call business functions you already have. Functions in existing C# or other programs can be registered as skills the model can call.
deepset-ai/haystack: Build production language-model and agent applications with modular pipelines. Retrieval, generation, and tools are replaceable components, so you can control the input and output of each step instead of hiding the whole chain in a black box. In production you can swap the retrieval or model component without rewriting the entire pipeline.
letta-ai/letta: A stateful agent platform, formerly MemGPT, focused on long-term memory. An agent can write important content into memory and read it back when needed, so a project can accumulate across many conversations. Open the same agent again a few days later, and it still remembers the key points it wrote down before.
modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk: The official Python SDK for the Model Context Protocol. You can use it to write tool servers that agents can call, or clients that connect to those tools, so different programs exchange capabilities in the same way. Tools you write can be called by other agents that support this protocol.
Skyvern-AI/skyvern: Uses AI to automate browser workflows such as filling forms, logging into admin backends, and moving data across several pages. It decides the next step from the page content, which suits sites that change often and flows that are hard to maintain with fixed scripts. After a site redesign, fixed selectors break easily, and this kind of flow is more stable.
yoheinakajima/babyagi: An early, well-known autonomous agent experiment. You give it a goal, and it keeps creating the next task, executing by priority, and turning the results into new tasks. The program itself is very short and mainly demonstrates this loop. It is now mostly read as a historical example, not a full-featured product.
camel-ai/camel: A multi-agent framework that uses role-play and conversation to make several agents collaborate. You can specify the stance of two or more roles and let them question each other and finish the task, rather than having one assistant answer in one direction. It suits trying multi-role debate and division of work before deciding whether to switch to a heavier framework.
pydantic/pydantic-ai: Build agents in Python with clear types. Inputs, tool parameters, and outputs can all be described with types, which makes it easier to connect different models and interfaces and reduces cases where the model returns a pile of text that does not match the structure. When model output does not match the type, it fails clearly so you can catch it.
openai/swarm: A lightweight multi-agent tutorial framework from OpenAI. It shows how to hand work from one agent to another, and the code is deliberately kept short, so it is for understanding handoffs rather than as a full production platform. OpenAI later released a newer agent SDK, and this one is kept as a lightweight demonstration.
AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui: A widely used Stable Diffusion web interface for generating and adjusting images from text on your own machine. You can install extensions, switch models, inpaint, and upscale without writing your own inference code. Models, extensions, and inpainting are all switched on the same page, and it is many people's local entry point for generating images.
Comfy-Org/ComfyUI: An interface and backend for building diffusion-model pipelines as node graphs. Each step, such as loading a model, the prompt, ControlNet, and the output, is a node, which suits image generation you need to repeat and whose flow you need to change. The same graph can be saved as a workflow and run again next time with a different prompt.
PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR: A lightweight OCR tool that can turn images and PDFs into structured text. It supports many languages and layouts, which suits extracting text from scans, screenshots, or tables without first training your own model. It can handle layout and tables, not only single lines of text.
opencv/opencv: An open-source computer vision library for reading images and video and for filters, features, and detection. Research and products both use it for low-level operations such as resizing, finding edges, and tracking objects, then pass the result to a higher-level model. When you write your own vision pipeline, reading and writing, geometry, and features usually go through it first.
tesseract-ocr/tesseract: A classic open-source optical character recognition engine that can extract text from images. It has a long history and many language packs, and it suits command-line use or embedding text recognition in other programs without necessarily calling a neural-network service. It can run without a graphics card, and it suits embedding in older systems for batch text recognition.
CompVis/stable-diffusion: The latent diffusion text-to-image model released by CompVis, and the base for a large number of later generation tools. You can generate images from a text description, and later web UIs, fine-tunes, and plugins mostly extended this direction. The paper and the weights are both here, so if you want to trace text-to-image back to its source, you start with this.
lllyasviel/Fooocus: Wraps Stable Diffusion into a simplified interface focused on prompts and image output. Many model and parameter choices are tucked away, so you mainly edit the sentence to generate an image without first understanding a whole node graph. If you want to tune fewer parameters and see an image sooner, it is easier to start with than a full node interface.
roboflow/supervision: A computer vision toolkit for handling detection results, annotation, and visualization. Boxes and classes returned by a model can be filtered, counted, and drawn on the frame here, so you can check whether a detection pipeline is usable. You can change the detection model and still keep the post-processing code for reuse.
upscayl/upscayl: A free desktop AI image upscaler for Linux, macOS, and Windows. You drag in a low-resolution image, and it uses a super-resolution model to enlarge it and fill in detail without you setting up a Python environment. You do not need to open a terminal: drag a photo into the desktop program and the upscale is done.
TencentARC/GFPGAN: A face restoration algorithm for real photographs, used to recover blurry or damaged faces. It tries to preserve identity while filling in facial detail, and it is commonly used to restore old photos and enhance low-resolution portraits. Old photos and low-resolution portraits are the main use, and landscape restoration is not its focus. The background outside the face is not the part it is responsible for restoring.
huggingface/pytorch-image-models: A large collection of PyTorch image backbone models, including training, evaluation, and pretrained weights. You can swap models such as ResNet and ViT through the same interface, for classification or as the backbone of other vision tasks. When you change backbones for an experiment, the training and evaluation scripts do not have to be rewritten each time.
xinntao/Real-ESRGAN: A practical image and video restoration model for upscaling and improving quality. It has corresponding models for real photographs and for anime, and it suits enlarging small images while reducing blur and compression artifacts. Photographs and anime need different weights, and the scale factor can be set separately. When the scale factor is too large, watch whether faces and text become distorted.
huggingface/diffusers: Hugging Face's diffusion model library for image, video, and audio generation in PyTorch. Loading a model, sampling, and attaching a scheduler all have ready-made flows, so you can put generation into your own program. Image, video, and audio generation can all be connected through the same loading method.
openai/CLIP: A model that places images and text in the same space and can judge how well a piece of text matches a picture. Image search, classification, and later generative models all use it to measure how close an image is to the sentence you described. For your own unlabeled image collection, you can search with a sentence in a zero-shot way.
lllyasviel/ControlNet: Controls a diffusion model with condition images such as edges, pose, and depth, so generation follows a specified structure. You can give it a line drawing or a skeleton, and the model generates according to that shape instead of freely following the text alone. Pose, line drawings, and depth can be used together, and the structure is more stable than text alone.
lovell/sharp: A high-performance Node.js image processing module that uses libvips for resizing and format conversion. Web services often use it to process uploaded images, and it uses less memory than decoding the whole image at once. After a website backend receives an uploaded image, thumbnails and format conversion are usually handed to it.
JaidedAI/EasyOCR: Ready-to-use optical character recognition that supports more than eighty languages and multiple writing systems. The call is simple, which suits projects that want to extract text from photos quickly without first compiling a traditional OCR engine. When a photo contains several writing systems, you do not have to install an engine for each language first.
invoke-ai/InvokeAI: A creation-oriented Stable Diffusion engine for generating and editing visual content. Besides text-to-image, it emphasizes the canvas, local edits, and the creative workflow, which suits people who want a full studio rather than only a prompt box. It is for staying on the canvas to edit the image, rather than having only a prompt input box.
nagadomi/waifu2x: Anime-style image super-resolution for enlarging images while reducing aliasing and noise. It is especially common for line art and illustrations, and it can enlarge small anime images more cleanly. Other models are a better fit for photograph super-resolution, and its strength is anime linework. When you enlarge an anime screenshot, the lines come out cleaner.
GraphiteEditor/Graphite: Community-developed 2D creative software that uses nodes for graphic design, digital drawing, and motion graphics. Tools and effects can be connected into a graph, which suits people who want an editor that is still in development and aimed at vector and procedural design. It is still in development, and it suits people who want to try node-based graphic design and keep using it.
black-forest-labs/flux: The official inference code for the Black Forest Labs FLUX.1 image model. You can use it to run FLUX text-to-image on your own machine, as an entry point to an image model a generation newer than early Stable Diffusion. It is the official inference entry point, and you can generate a comparison image with it before connecting your own pipeline.
junyanz/pytorch-CycleGAN-and-pix2pix: A PyTorch implementation of image-to-image translation, including CycleGAN and pix2pix. It can do translations such as style transfer, season change, and sketch-to-photo with paired or unpaired data. Use pix2pix when you have paired data, and use CycleGAN when you only have two sets of images in different styles.
danielgatis/rembg: A tool that uses AI to remove image backgrounds automatically. It can be used from the command line or as a library, separating a person, a product, or another subject from the background and outputting a transparent background for later compositing. Product shots and portraits can both be exported with a transparent background, then passed to compositing or an online-store layout. After background removal, it is best to check the hair and semi-transparent edges.
Sanster/IOPaint: An AI image inpainting tool that can remove objects or redraw a chosen region with text and a diffusion model. You paint over the part you do not want, and the model fills it in from the surrounding picture or a prompt, without manual clone stamping. Removing passersby and redrawing a region from text can both be done in the same tool.
sczhou/CodeFormer: A face restoration model that uses a codebook to recover damaged or low-resolution facial detail. You can trade off fidelity against restoration strength so a face is not restored into a completely different person. If restoration is too strong it changes the likeness, so you set the fidelity yourself. Low-resolution ID photos and old portraits are both common uses.
ImageMagick/ImageMagick: An image toolkit that handles more than two hundred formats and can convert, edit, and composite from the command line. Batch thumbnails, format conversion, adding text, and montages all use it, and it is the underlying tool in many automated flows. For scripts and server-side batch image processing, it is still the most common command-line tool.
lukas-blecher/LaTeX-OCR: Turns images of mathematical formulas into LaTeX code. Photograph or screenshot a formula and you get editable source, which suits organizing equations in notes, papers, and scans. Handwritten and printed formulas can both be tried, and complex layouts need further manual editing. The generated code should still be pasted back into a compiler to check.
CompVis/latent-diffusion: Research code for high-resolution latent diffusion models, and the predecessor implementation of Stable Diffusion. It demonstrates doing diffusion in a compressed space and then decoding into an image, an approach later text-to-image models carried on. If you want to understand why Stable Diffusion does diffusion in latent space, start with this code.
python-pillow/Pillow: A Python image processing library for opening files, resizing, drawing, and converting formats. Almost every Python image program reads and writes files through it, then passes the pixels to a model or saves the result. Opening and saving files before and after a model is, in Python, usually done through it.
darktable-org/darktable: Open-source photo workflow and RAW development software for organizing and color-grading photos. You can manage a photo library and make non-destructive adjustments to RAW files, as an open-source alternative to commercial development software. Adjustments are written to a side record, so the original photo is not overwritten. Color-grading steps can be copied to the other photos in the same set.
instantX-research/InstantID: Identity-preserving generation from a single reference image, keeping the same person in a new picture. When you change the pose, scene, or style, the face still matches the reference photo, without first training a model for each person. One photo is enough, and you do not have to collect dozens of photos of the same person and train first. With more profile views and occlusion, identity drifts more easily.
libvips/libvips: A low-memory, high-speed image processing library. It processes large images as needed, and server-side thumbnails and format conversion often choose it instead of loading an entire high-resolution image into memory at once. When processing very large images it does not have to decode the whole image, which is why servers choose it. When a thumbnail service has many users, the memory advantage is more noticeable.
lllyasviel/stable-diffusion-webui-forge: A high-efficiency fork of Stable Diffusion WebUI, optimized for speed and newer models. The interface is close to the original WebUI, but it puts more weight on memory and on inference efficiency for newer-generation models. When GPU memory is tight, or you need to run a newer model, this fork is one to consider.
bmaltais/kohya_ss: A graphical interface for training LoRA and fine-tuning diffusion models. You prepare a set of images, train a small set of weights, then use them in WebUI or ComfyUI to lock in a character, an art style, or an object. Dataset organization and training parameters are both set in the graphical interface, so you do not have to rely only on the command line.
NVlabs/stylegan2: NVIDIA's StyleGAN2, which synthesizes high-resolution images with a generative adversarial network. It is known for high-quality synthesis of categories such as faces, and it is the base code for much later GAN editing and latent-space research. Latent vectors can be used for further editing experiments, and it is a common starting point for GAN face research.
Acly/krita-ai-diffusion: An AI drawing plugin for Krita that can inpaint and outpaint from a selection and a prompt. You stay inside the drawing software to edit the picture, without exporting it to another generation interface and pasting it back. Painters can use generation while staying inside Krita's layers and selections.
lllyasviel/IC-Light: A tool for controlling the lighting of a generated image. It can change light direction and environment while trying to keep the subject. It suits relighting an image so it looks placed in another scene, rather than resampling the whole picture. The subject is kept and only the light changes, which suits product photos and portraits when you change the ambient light.
yt-dlp/yt-dlp: A full-featured command-line audio and video downloader that can save video and audio from a large number of sites. You can choose the format, subtitles, and playlists, which suits people who need to archive or further process online video. It is updated frequently after sites change, and it is the mainstream choice for command-line downloading now. Playlists and subtitles can be saved in one pass.
obsproject/obs-studio: Free, open-source live streaming and screen recording software. It can mix screens, cameras, windows, and audio, then switch scenes, which suits livestreaming, teaching, and recording tutorials without buying separate capture software. Scenes can be arranged in advance and switched with one click during a stream. Teaching, livestreaming, and screen recording can share the same set of scenes.
remotion-dev/remotion: Make videos programmatically with React, for repeatable animation and templates. The picture is written as components, and when the data changes a new version can be rendered, which suits batch production of intros, charts, and social videos. The same video can be batch-rendered into many versions from data, for example one clip per person.
FFmpeg/FFmpeg: A core tool for audio and video, handling transcoding, cutting, streaming, and format conversion. Players, editing software, and website backends often call it for the actual decoding and encoding. When you write your own editing or streaming tool, the lower layer almost always calls it. Almost all audio and video software ends up calling it.
jellyfin/jellyfin: A free-software media system you can host yourself to organize and play video. You control the library, subtitles, and multiple clients, and it is used as a home media server without putting the library on a commercial platform. Several devices at home can play your own library, and you manage the accounts and metadata yourself.
mpv-player/mpv: A lightweight, high-quality command-line media player. It supports many formats and shaders, playback can be controlled by keyboard and scripts, and other interfaces often wrap it. Shaders and scripts can change the playback look, while the interface is usually wrapped separately. Configuration files can be synced to several computers.
ATH-MaaS/Pixelle-Video: An AI automatic short-video engine that goes from content all the way to a finished video. You can start from text or source material and let the pipeline handle the script, the visuals, and the output, shortening the time spent across many tools to make one short video. The short-video steps are chained together, so the script, the visuals, and the output do not each use a separate program.
hpcaitech/Open-Sora: An open-source video generation project aimed at lowering the barrier to high-quality text-to-video. It provides models and training and inference code so research and creative work can try text-to-video on open weights. If you want to change training or inference rather than only use a ready-made website, look at this open project.
Stability-AI/generative-models: Stability AI's generative model code, including image-to-video models such as Stable Video Diffusion. You can generate a short video starting from a single image, and it is also the official code collection for several of their generative models. Stable Video Diffusion for image-to-video and the code for the other generative models are both collected here.
HandBrake/HandBrake: An open-source video transcoding tool for compressing and converting to common formats. It has a graphical interface where you can choose device presets, which suits turning large files into versions that are easy to play or upload. Presets match common devices, so after conversion you can play or upload directly. When batch-converting, you can keep using the same preset.
k4yt3x/video2x: Video super-resolution and frame interpolation with machine learning. It can enlarge low-resolution video or raise the frame rate, so old footage and animation show less aliasing and stutter on a large screen. Upscaling and frame interpolation can be done separately, and both old animation and source video can be used. Models can be chosen separately for animation or live action.
bloc97/Anime4K: A real-time anime video upscaling algorithm that can improve quality during playback. It focuses on lines and flat color, which suits enlarging anime while you watch without first re-rendering the whole video offline. A player can apply it in real time, without first rendering a new file. Players such as mpv can attach this algorithm directly.
HBAI-Ltd/Toonflow-app: An open-source tool for short dramas and comic dramas, covering scripts, storyboards, characters and scenes, and image and video generation. The preproduction and visual steps a short video needs can move forward inside the same project. A short drama goes from script to picture, and the storyboards and characters in between can stay in the same project. Character settings can be carried into later storyboards.
KlingAIResearch/LivePortrait: Turns a single portrait into a moving portrait animation. You use one photo as the identity, then drive expressions and head movement, which suits portraits that talk or turn their head without first filming a video. A single portrait is enough, and the driving comes from another motion or expression clip.
Wan-Video/Wan2.2: An open-source large video generation model in Alibaba's Wan series. It can generate video conditioned on text or an image, with open weights and inference code, which makes it easier for research and further development to connect to your own pipeline. Open weights make it easy to connect it to your own editing or generation pipeline and try it.
lllyasviel/FramePack: Makes generation with video diffusion models more practical by lowering the memory pressure of long clips. It changes how frames are processed so a longer generation does not have to keep the state of every frame on the GPU at once. This way of handling frames becomes practically useful when the GPU cannot hold a long video.
storytold/filmcraft: Open-source nonlinear video editing software written from scratch in Rust. The direction is a local tool that can edit and organize a timeline, rather than wrapping another layer around an existing editing engine. It is for people who want to look at a timeline newly written in Rust, rather than another wrap around an existing editing core.
duixcom/Duix-Avatar: An open-source digital-human tool that can be used offline to generate talking-head videos and clone digital humans. You can do lip sync and appearance on your own machine, which suits talking-head workflows where you do not want to send the voice and portrait to the cloud. Talking-head videos can be produced offline, which suits people who do not want to send portraits and voices to the cloud.

genmoai/mochi: Genmo's open-source text-to-video model. mrdoob/three.js: Create and render 3D scenes in the browser with JavaScript. pixijs/pixijs: A fast 2D WebGL rendering engine for interactive graphics and visual effects. pmndrs/react-three-fiber: A renderer for writing Three.js scenes in the React style. 3D objects can be written as components, and the picture updates when state changes, which makes it easier to put 3D into an existing React interface. BabylonJS/Babylon.js: A full-featured web 3D rendering and game engine. graphdeco-inria/gaussian-splatting: The original implementation of 3D Gaussian Splatting. blender/blender: The official Blender source code, covering modeling, animation, compositing, video editing, and rendering. bkaradzic/bgfx: A cross-graphics-API rendering library that lets your own engine target OpenGL, Direct3D, Vulkan, and Metal. NVlabs/instant-ngp: NVIDIA's instant neural graphics primitives, which greatly speed up training and rendering of NeRF-style scenes. playcanvas/engine: A web graphics engine built on WebGL, WebGPU, and glTF. It loads 3D scenes and runs interaction in the browser, and the editor ecosystem is built around this runtime core. Scenes load through glTF, and both the editor and the runtime are built around this core.
bulletphysics/bullet3: A real-time collision detection and physics library, commonly used in visual effects, games, and robotics. isl-org/Open3D: A modern 3D data processing library for point clouds, meshes, and visualization. Scan data can be filtered, registered, and reconstructed here, and both Python and C++ can call it. Cleaning and registration of scanned point clouds can be finished in Python and then visualized.
assimp/assimp: Reads more than forty 3D file formats into one data structure. alicevision/Meshroom: A node-based photogrammetry tool that reconstructs a 3D model from photos. nerfstudio-project/nerfstudio: A workbench for research on novel-view synthesis. NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting (splatfacto) can share the same data, training, and viewing tools. Switching methods does not require rewriting the whole set of scripts, which suits trying Gaussian reconstruction.
playcanvas/supersplat: A tool for editing 3D Gaussian splats in the browser. facebookresearch/pytorch3d: A component library for 3D deep learning with PyTorch. Meshes, cameras, and differentiable rendering can go into a training pipeline. carson-katri/dream-textures: Stable Diffusion built into Blender, so you can generate textures directly in the scene. opentoonz/opentoonz: A full-featured open-source 2D animation production program. PixarAnimationStudios/OpenUSD: Pixar's Universal Scene Description, for exchanging 3D scenes between different programs. cnr-isti-vclab/meshlab: An open-source mesh processing system for cleaning, repairing, and viewing 3D models. nerfstudio-project/gsplat: A CUDA-accelerated Gaussian Splatting rasterization library for research and integration. shader-slang/slang: A shading language that makes shaders easier to write and easier to compile across platforms. mitsuba-renderer/mitsuba3: A retargetable forward and inverse renderer for research-grade physically based rendering. AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr: The high-dynamic-range EXR image format widely used in the film industry, and its reference implementation. AcademySoftwareFoundation/MaterialX: An open standard for exchanging material and look descriptions between different programs and renderers. AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenColorIO: A color management framework for visual effects and animation. openbq-org/OpenBB: An open-source financial data platform for analysts, quant researchers, and AI agents. akfamily/akshare: An open-source financial data interface for fetching stocks, macro data, and other market data in Python. myhhub/stock: A Chinese-language stock tool that includes quotes, indicators, chart patterns, stock screening, backtesting, and automated trading. facebookresearch/vggt-omega: A follow-on model to VGGT that continues to do feed-forward 3D geometry from images with a Transformer. TencentARC/InstantMesh: A sparse-view large reconstruction model that efficiently generates a 3D mesh from a single image. dreamgaussian/dreamgaussian: It makes 3D content with generative Gaussian Splatting, quickly producing an object from an image or text and then extracting a mesh. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2.1: Hunyuan3D 2.1 generates high-fidelity 3D assets from images, with production-ready PBR materials. facebookresearch/map-anything: General feed-forward metric 3D reconstruction that estimates real-scale geometry and cameras from images. AiuniAI/Unique3D: It efficiently generates a high-quality 3D mesh from a single image. The model looks after both multi-view consistency and surface detail, which suits needing an object you can open immediately rather than only a point cloud. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-1: The first generation of Hunyuan3D puts text-to-3D and image-to-3D in the same framework. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
naver/mast3r: It does 3D image matching on top of DUSt3R, so corresponding points have a geometric basis. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
cvlab-columbia/zero123: From one image it zero-shot imagines how an object looks from a new viewpoint. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
deepseek-ai/DreamCraft3D: Hierarchical 3D generation: a diffusion prior first sets the overall shape, then quality and detail are raised. From text or an image you can get a more complete object rather than only a rough shape. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
wgsxm/PartCrafter: It generates structured 3D meshes by part. An object is split into separable parts instead of one fused surface, which makes later modification, materials, or joints easier. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
3DTopia/LGM: A large multi-view Gaussian model that quickly generates high-resolution 3D content from images. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
SUDO-AI-3D/zero123plus: A diffusion base model that generates consistent multiple views from a single image. Style and shape stay more aligned across the new angles, and you can then attach a reconstruction program to turn them into a mesh or a Gaussian scene. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
Stability-AI/stable-fast-3d: It quickly reconstructs a 3D mesh from a single image, and at the same time does UV unwrapping and lighting separation. The surface can be textured directly, which suits assets that need to go to a DCC tool or a game. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
VAST-AI-Research/TripoSG: High-fidelity 3D shape synthesis with large-scale rectified flow. From an image it can produce cleaner geometry, with the emphasis on shape quality rather than only speed. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
Totoro97/NeuS: It reconstructs objects with a neural implicit surface, combining volume rendering and surface constraints. Multi-view photos can yield a more accurate mesh, and it is a reference for many later surface-reconstruction codebases. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
One-2-3-45/One-2-3-45: Any single image becomes a 3D mesh in about 45 seconds, without a long extra optimization for each shape. It first generates multiple views, then reconstructs, and it is an early practical single-image-to-mesh pipeline. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
guochengqian/Magic123: It uses 2D and 3D diffusion priors together to generate a high-quality 3D object from one image. The 2D model fills in appearance, and the 3D prior holds the geometry, reducing wild guesses on the back. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
thu-ml/prolificdreamer: It uses variational score distillation to generate high-fidelity and diverse 3D content from text. The same description can produce more than one look, and the quality is also higher than early DreamFusion-style methods. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
Roblox/cube: Roblox's foundation model for 3D intelligence, used to understand and generate 3D content. It can help turn an image or a description into scenes and assets for pipelines such as game production. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
DreamTechAI/Direct3D-S2: Large-scale 3D generation with spatial sparse attention, which makes high-resolution generation easier. It can output 3D directly from a condition, without densely computing the whole volume in one pass. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
YuliangXiu/ECON: It reconstructs a clothed human body in 3D from a single portrait and refines the surface with normal integration. The point is that clothing folds are kept together with the body, rather than only a naked template. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
Stability-AI/stable-point-aware-3d: It reconstructs a 3D object from a single image while using point-cloud information to stabilize the shape. Geometry and appearance are handled separately, reducing the flattening and missing backs common with a single view. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
YuliangXiu/ICON: It reconstructs a clothed human body from a single image and normals. The implicit surface follows the clothing outline instead of forcing a standard body shape, and it is a commonly used codebase for this kind of human digitization. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
3DTopia/OpenLRM: An open-source implementation of a large reconstruction model that feed-forward produces 3D from a single image or a few images. Inference is fast, which suits batch-converting product photos or character images into rotatable assets. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
facebookresearch/pifuhd: High-resolution 3D human digitization from a single portrait. A pixel-aligned implicit function can preserve hair and clothing detail, and it is a frequently cited codebase for single-image human reconstruction. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
bennyguo/instant-nsr-pl: Neural surface reconstruction based on Instant-NGP that can train NeuS-style methods in about ten minutes. Multi-view photos can yield a mesh more quickly, which suits research on surface reconstruction. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
ashawkey/nerf2mesh: It recovers a fine textured mesh from a NeRF and adaptively densifies the surface. A novel-view scene can be handed back to traditional rendering as a mesh, instead of leaving only a neural field. From a flat image or text you get a 3D asset you can rotate and look at, then pass it to a rendering or game pipeline.
unslothai/unsloth: A local interface for running and fine-tuning language models and diffusion models. It supports GGUF, MLX, FLUX, and others, so you can train image models on your own machine without a cloud service. When you try a new model, you do not have to rewrite the whole training script each time.
mudler/LocalAI: An open-source local AI engine that can run language models, vision, speech, images, and video on your own machine. It works without a GPU, and one interface replaces several cloud APIs. Image generation and inference can both stay on your own machine. Data does not have to be uploaded outside.
ahujasid/mcp-for-blender: A community plugin for controlling 3D operations inside Blender with any language model. You can ask the model to help with modeling and scene edits, and it is not affiliated with the official Blender Foundation. Commands are turned into operations inside Blender.
Anil-matcha/Open-Generative-AI: A self-hosted image and video generation studio that integrates models such as FLUX, Kling, Sora, and Veo. It is for generating images and video locally, under the MIT license. Models can be swapped for interfaces you already have.
taichi-dev/taichi: A language and compiler for writing high-performance GPU programs in Python. It suits computer graphics, physics simulation, and differentiable computing, and the same program can run on different graphics cards. When researching rendering and simulation, you can write less low-level GPU code.
stefan-jansen/machine-learning-for-tradi: Code for the third edition of Machine Learning for Trading. It goes from fetching market data, features, and models through to backtesting and live execution, for learning the whole quantitative trading workflow. The notebooks follow the book chapter by chapter.
deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness: The official agent harness from DeepSeek, whose architecture treats everything as a plugin. It uses Cordis to assemble tools and interfaces into swappable parts, and you can open a web interface locally with npx. It is still a development preview, and the plugin interface may change later.
NousResearch/hermes-agent: An autonomous agent from Nous Research that writes experience it has used into skills and remembers who you are. It can run on an inexpensive server, a GPU cluster, or an idle setup that costs almost nothing. A new conversation looks back through the old record, so you do not have to introduce yourself from scratch every time.
khoj-ai/khoj: A self-hosted personal AI second brain. It finds answers on the web and in your documents, and you can also build custom agents, schedule automation, and do deep research. It can connect to local or online language models and can generate images, and the data can stay on your own machine.
ssloy/tinyrenderer: A short computer graphics course that writes a small renderer from scratch in C++. Following the lessons, you implement rasterization, shading, and texturing yourself, for people who want to understand how a picture is drawn rather than only calling a ready-made engine. The code is short, so you can read line by line how the rendering is done.
questdb/questdb: A high-performance open-source time-series database for storing and querying timestamped data such as market data. Queries are fast and latency is low, and it supports Parquet and data formats commonly used in capital markets. It suits market-data storage for a trading system, and it is not an automatic order-placing strategy.
camenduru/stable-diffusion-webui-colab: A set of Google Colab notebooks for running Stable Diffusion WebUI on Colab. You can try text-to-image and DreamBooth without first building a GPU environment yourself. The notebooks are assembled by the community, and you still have to check the model weights and licenses yourself.
firecrawl/firecrawl: An open-source crawler that turns web pages into clean Markdown for an AI agent to use. It can crawl a whole site and extract structured data without writing a selector for every website. It suits people who need to bring web data into an agent.
vercel/satori: A library from Vercel that turns HTML and CSS into an SVG image. A common use is generating Open Graph preview images without opening a browser to take a screenshot. It produces images by layout, and it is not a diffusion model that generates a picture from text.
krillinai/OpenCreator: An open-source creation workbench formerly known as KrillinAI. It is for downloading video, translation, and dubbing, and in the same place an agent can make video, images, audio, and avatars. It suits social content such as YouTube and TikTok.
OpenByteInc/QuantDinger: A self-hosted quantitative research platform. It turns a trading idea into a Python strategy, then runs backtests, paper trading, and live trading across stocks, cryptocurrency, and forex. The focus is researching and executing strategies, and it is not a ready-made automatic stock-picking signal.
HKUDS/ViMax: A multi-agent video generation system from the University of Hong Kong. A director, screenwriter, producer, and storyboard artist divide the work, and it can take an idea or a script through to a full video. It pushes text through to a watchable video rather than only producing a prompt. Each role handles one stage, so you can change only the script or only the picture.
stablyai/orca: An agent IDE for desktop and phone. It runs several coding agents, such as Codex and Claude Code, side by side, each in its own git worktree. You can use your own subscription and follow progress in the terminal, on a remote machine, and on a phone.
divamgupta/diffusionbee-stable-diffusion: A desktop app for running Stable Diffusion locally on an M1 Mac, with one-click install, so you do not have to assemble the dependencies yourself. It generates images on your own machine, for people who do not want to set up a Python environment first. The model and the generation both stay on the local machine.
junyanz/CycleGAN: Classic code for unpaired image translation. It can turn a painting into a photo, a horse into a zebra, or transfer style. The two domains do not need paired, aligned training images, which suits trying how a generative adversarial network changes image appearance. The paper and the code are both public, so you can read them against the implementation.
jub0t/Concat: A local-first open-source video editor meant to replace CapCut. It supports multi-track editing, subtitles, text-to-speech, and background removal, and a Rust engine runs it on your own machine. Clips do not have to be uploaded, and you can also script it over JSON-RPC and MCP.
je-suis-tm/quant-trading: A set of Python quantitative strategy examples, including pairs trading, options, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and breakouts. It shows how each strategy computes a signal from data, and it is not a platform that can place live orders right away. You can pick one strategy, change it, and backtest it yourself.
NVlabs/Sana: NVIDIA's efficient diffusion model uses linear attention to generate high-resolution images with less computation, and it also includes SANA-Video and a streaming version. It is for generating images and video, for people who want to run a lighter diffusion model on their own machine.
domlysz/BlenderGIS: A Blender add-on for bringing geographic data into a 3D scene. It can pull basemaps, digital elevation, and map geometry, and build terrain and real-world scenery inside Blender, without first converting files in another GIS program. It suits map visualization and scene layout.
paperclipai/paperclip: An open-source agent orchestrator for managing a team of AI coworkers. You can set goals, assign roles and budgets, then track the work and the cost in one interface. Each agent can use a different model, and tasks and permissions stay on a server you host yourself.
openvinotoolkit/openvino: Intel's open-source inference toolkit for optimizing and deploying models that are already trained, not for training a new model. It can convert vision and diffusion models into a format that runs faster on a CPU or a GPU, and it is not a drawing program that generates images from text. It suits people who want to run a model on their own machine.
Baiyuetribe/paper2gui: An install-free AI desktop toolbox that wraps models from papers into interfaces you can open and use immediately. It covers painting, speech synthesis, video frame interpolation and super-resolution, accompaniment separation, and subtitles. It is for trying these tools on your own machine without setting up an environment for each project.
lucidrains/imagen-pytorch: A PyTorch implementation of Google Imagen for text-to-image. It is for researching and running text-to-image, and the repository also has experiments related to text-to-video. It suits people who want to read the code and see how a diffusion model turns text into an image.
cantaro86/Financial-Models-Numerical-Met: A set of quantitative-finance notebooks that use Python to cover option pricing, the Heston model, Brownian motion, and numerical methods. They are for understanding how the models compute prices and risk, not a trading program that can place orders right away. You can change the parameters and recalculate them yourself.
NVIDIA/pix2pixHD: NVIDIA's high-resolution conditional generative adversarial network. It synthesizes 2048 by 1024 images from label maps or other conditions, and it can also manipulate existing images. It suits people who want high-resolution image translation in computer-graphics and vision experiments.
thedotmack/claude-mem: A cross-conversation agent memory plugin. It records the tools and methods used in each session, compresses them, and injects the relevant context on the next turn. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and others, so the agent does not treat the project as new every time.
phillipi/pix2pix: A classic program that uses conditional generative adversarial networks for image-to-image translation. It suits people who want to read the paper's implementation and see how conditional generation changes an image. The program is written in Lua.
RunanywhereAI/runanywhere-sdks: A toolkit for running AI locally on phones, in the browser, and on the desktop. Language models, vision, speech, and image generation can stay on the device, without sending data to the cloud. It is for offline inference, not a standalone drawing website. Eight platforms share the same calling style.
nadermx/backgroundremover: An open-source command-line tool that removes backgrounds from images and video. The output can be passed to editing software, and the files stay on the machine.
yi1108/printfilm: A creation platform for AI short films and comic dramas. You can go from copy to a storyboard, reference images, image-to-video, and then a composite preview. hugo2046/QuantsPlaybook: A quantitative-research collection that reproduces brokers' quantitative research reports in Python notebooks. You can change the data and recalculate it yourself.
charliedream1/ai_quant_trade: A one-stop set of notes and programs for learning stock AI and trading. It is for learning the whole workflow, not a signal that guarantees a profit.
unclecode/crawl4ai: An open-source crawler that turns any website into clean Markdown suitable for a language model. You can host it yourself and then pass the result to an AI agent as data. cheaper-inference/OmniRoute: A self-hosted AI gateway. One interface connects many model providers, and Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others can point here. Stability-AI/StableStudio: A generative-image interface maintained by the Stability AI community, and the open-source front end of DreamStudio. LykosAI/StabilityMatrix: A cross-platform package manager for Stable Diffusion. It installs and switches interfaces such as Automatic1111 and ComfyUI, and keeps models and settings in one place. modelscope/FunClip: A video-editing tool based on FunASR. It does speech-to-text, generates subtitles, and uses a language model to help choose clips. amagine-ai/Amagine3D: An open-source tool that generates editable 3D designs from a product description, reference images, and dimensions. It turns requirements into CAD you can edit, rather than only producing an image that looks three-dimensional.
heygen-com/hyperframes: HeyGen's open-source video rendering framework. You write the frames with HTML, CSS, and animation, then export a stable MP4. FoundationVision/VAR: The official implementation of a NeurIPS 2024 best paper. PaddlePaddle/PaddleGAN: Baidu PaddlePaddle's GAN application library. If you want to try several classic effects at once, you can start here.
achannarasappa/ticker: A small terminal tool for watching live quotes and positions in stocks, cryptocurrencies, and derivatives. PyPortfolio/PyPortfolioOpt: A Python library for portfolio optimization. It can compute the efficient frontier, Black-Litterman, and hierarchical risk parity, and it helps set weights from expected returns and risk. It is for studying how to allocate positions, not an order-placing program.
Mathieu2301/TradingView-API: An unofficial library for reading live quotes and chart data from TradingView. You can connect it as a data source for your own monitoring or backtests. It is not TradingView's official API, and it does not replace placing orders through a broker.
MochiDiffusion/MochiDiffusion: A native Mac program for running Stable Diffusion, written in Swift and Core ML, and able to use the Apple Neural Engine. It generates images on your own Mac without installing a Python environment first. The model and the generations both stay on the machine.
WyattBlue/auto-editor: An automatic editing tool that detects silence and still frames, then joins the segments that have content. Anil-matcha/AI-Youtube-Shorts-Generator: An open-source tool that cuts long videos into vertical shorts.
