freqtrade/freqtrade-strategies: A library of strategy examples for the Freqtrade trading bot. It contains buy and sell rules shared by other people, which you can take for backtesting and research. It is for seeing how strategies are written, not a set of signals that guarantee a profit and can go live right away. You need to verify each strategy yourself.
google/tf-quant-finance: Google's quantitative-finance library, written in TensorFlow. It is for pricing, risk, and numerical computation, and it can run on a GPU. It suits research into how financial models can be sped up, not a program for placing orders or picking stocks.
bojieli/ai-agent-book: The open-source repository for Bojie Li's Understanding AI Agents in Depth. It includes the full text, a PDF, and companion code by chapter. It is for reading memory, tools, and engineering practice alongside the design principles, not a ready-to-install agent product. You can start by modifying the code for a particular chapter.
TheLastBen/fast-stable-diffusion: TheLastBen's Stable Diffusion notebooks and DreamBooth workflow. They are for running Automatic1111, ComfyUI, and fine-tuning more quickly on Colab or on a local machine. The environment and commonly used models are wired up in advance, which suits people who want to spend less time assembling dependencies.
leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp: An inference program that runs diffusion models in pure C/C++, with support for SD, Flux, Wan, and others. It does not need a full Python deep-learning framework. It is for generating images and image-to-image on your own machine, and models can be quantized and then run locally.
JerBouma/FinanceToolkit: A Python library for transparent financial analysis. It can pull financial statements, compute ratios, and compare factors. It suits research into company fundamentals, not an automatic order-placing trading program. Data sources and calculations can be traced. You can switch the data source and recalculate.
ssloy/tinyraytracer: A short ray-tracing course that writes a small renderer from scratch in C++. As you follow the lessons, you implement ray-scene intersection yourself. Together with the author's tinyrenderer, it is a series of graphics courses, for people who want to understand how light is computed into an image.
NVIDIAGameWorks/kaolin: NVIDIA's PyTorch library for accelerating 3D deep learning. It includes tools related to cameras, differentiable rendering, and Gaussian splatting. It is for 3D research and training, not a standalone scene viewer. You can connect your own data and models.
getopenscreen/openscreen: An open-source screen recorder for product demo videos. It supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, with GPU acceleration and no watermark or subscription. Clips stay on your own machine. It suits people who need to produce demos and do not want a closed-source recording tool.
HKUDS/DeepTutor: A personalized tutoring agent from the University of Hong Kong. It provides long-term coaching, research, and interactive practice matched to your level, and you can host it yourself. The point is that it keeps remembering learning progress, rather than being a chat window that only answers one question. Teaching materials and conversations can both stay on your own machine.
siyuan-note/siyuan: A self-hosted, privacy-first knowledge workspace. Notes are stored as Markdown on your own machine, and people and AI agents can organize and search them together. It is for a personal knowledge base, rather than handing notes to an outside service.
XavierXiao/Dreambooth-Stable-Diffusion: An implementation of the DreamBooth paper with Stable Diffusion. It fine-tunes a model on a small number of photos so the model learns a specific subject. It is for researching and running text-to-image fine-tuning, not a ready-made drawing website.
cloneofsimo/lora: An early implementation that fine-tunes diffusion models quickly with low-rank adaptation. Training only a small part of the weights can add a new style or subject to Stable Diffusion. It suits people who want to fine-tune it themselves without retraining the whole model.
hudson-and-thames/mlfinlab: A toolkit for financial machine learning. It covers common steps in labeling, features, portfolios, and backtesting, so you can study how a strategy is trained on data. It is an analysis tool, not an automatic order-placing trading program. Each calculation can be checked against the formula.
darkzOGx/youtube-automation-agent: A self-hosted video agent. It writes a script, voiceover, and visuals from a topic, publishes only after you approve, and then adjusts the next video from the data. The model interface can be swapped. You have to confirm the finished video and the publishing yourself. The script and the finished video can stay on your own machine for further edits.
hku-mars/FAST-LIVO2: LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry from the MaRS Lab at the University of Hong Kong. It quickly estimates how the camera and the LiDAR move, reconstructs a colored point cloud, and also involves Gaussian splatting. It suits research on robot localization and 3D reconstruction. The code follows the paper, so you can read the implementation alongside it.
nexu-io/html-video: A tool that renders HTML, CSS, and data into an MP4 on your own computer. A coding assistant can ask it to produce a video. It has ready-made templates and a swappable rendering engine. It is for programmatic video, not pay-per-render cloud rendering. The video file stays on your computer.
advimman/lama: LaMa uses Fourier convolutions for large-area image inpainting, so a large masked region can still be filled from the surrounding texture. If the resolution changes, it does not need retraining, so removing a large object or filling a large hole is more stable than older methods that only look locally. If you want to erase a large patch in the middle of the frame, this is a common starting point.
geekyutao/Inpaint-Anything: One click outlines an object, and segmentation and inpainting models then remove it, fill it, or replace it from text. You do not paint the mask yourself. Images, video, and 3D scenes each have a corresponding workflow, which suits clearing away pedestrians and clutter or swapping one object for another. Selection and redrawing are separate, so the whole image is not changed together.
lxfater/inpaint-web: Image inpainting and upscaling in the browser, running locally with WebGPU and WASM, so images do not have to be uploaded. Paint over a flaw and it is filled from the surroundings, and you can upscale at the same time. It suits people who do not want to install Python first and want the files to stay on their own computer. Opening the page is enough to use it.
Bing-su/adetailer: A Stable Diffusion WebUI extension that uses a detection model to outline a region automatically and then redraws it locally, mostly faces and hands by default. If the details break after an image is generated, you can redraw only that spot without painting a mask by hand, while the composition and the other areas stay as they were. Faces and fingers are the parts most often repaired this way.
lkwq007/stablediffusion-infinity: Outpainting on an infinite canvas with Stable Diffusion. You start from one image and keep generating toward the edges, so the picture can keep extending without deciding the final size in advance. This is outpainting more than filling holes, and it suits people who want to widen a composition or lengthen a scene. The canvas has no fixed boundary.
JiahuiYu/generative_inpainting: The official code for DeepFill v1 and v2, which fills irregular holes with contextual attention and gated convolution. The model looks at the image around the hole to decide what to fill in, rather than smearing nearby pixels together. These are classic implementations from CVPR 2018 and ICCV 2019, and they are now often used as research baselines for comparison.
knazeri/edge-connect: It first predicts the edges of the missing region, then fills color and texture along those lines. Building and object outlines are easier to keep, so the fill does not become a structureless patch of color. This is structure-guided inpainting from ICCV 2019. Lines are fixed first and color is filled afterward, so hard-edged objects look more natural.
andreas128/RePaint: Image inpainting with a denoising diffusion model, without training a new network just to fill holes. An existing diffusion model can repeatedly redraw the gap according to the mask, while known regions stay as they were. CVPR 2022. If you already have a generative model, you can use it to repair the image without training a separate inpainting network.
TencentARC/BrushNet: A pluggable diffusion inpainting model that uses separate dual branches for the mask and the original image. It can attach to an existing text-to-image model and redraw the brushed region without retraining the whole base model. ECCV 2024. If you want to keep the original diffusion model, adding one inpainting branch is enough.
scraed/LanPaint: A training-free inpainting sampler that can be applied to existing diffusion and rectified-flow models. Inside the mask it takes a few extra steps before denoising, spending more compute for a more stable fill, and it also supports replacing a local region from text. It has a ComfyUI node. The method itself is a sampling paper, not only a node package. TMLR.
open-mmlab/PowerPaint: One model handles several kinds of image inpainting at once: inserting an object from text, removing an object, outpainting, and guidance by shape. Changing the task prompt is enough, so you do not install a separate model for removal and for redrawing. ECCV 2024. The same weights can change purpose, so removing and adding objects does not require swapping weights.
fenglinglwb/MAT: Large-hole image inpainting with a Transformer. The mask affects attention, so the model knows where to generate and where to keep. When a large area is missing, distant texture can be aligned, instead of relying only on a few pixels at the edge of the hole. It suits gaps so large that ordinary convolution cannot see the whole context.
Picsart-AI-Research/MI-GAN: A mobile-oriented image-inpainting baseline that uses distillation and reparameterization to compress the model so it can run on a mobile device. The emphasis is that the image still looks clear after an object is removed, without relying on a desktop-class GPU. ICCV 2023. If you want erasure on a phone, this is more practical than a large desktop model.
DQiaole/ZITS_inpainting: Structure-enhanced image inpainting from CVPR 2022. It first restores lines and edges step by step, then fills texture with mask position encoding, so buildings and regular objects do not end up warped. When the gap contains straight lines or outlines, the structure is restored first and the color is filled afterward.
lyndonzheng/Pluralistic-Inpainting: The same gap can be filled in several ways that are all plausible, rather than returning only one answer. When the hole is large and more than one content would be reasonable, you can pick the one that fits the picture best. This is pluralistic image completion from CVPR 2019. It does not force every image to have only one way of being filled.
researchmm/AOT-GAN-for-Inpainting: High-resolution image inpainting with aggregated contextual transformations, looking around the gap at several scales together. It aligns texture in a large image more easily than single-scale convolution, and it suits high-resolution photos that need a region filled. This is an image-inpainting program from TVCG 2023. When filling a high-resolution image, fine and coarse scales are used together.
open-mmlab/mmagic: OpenMMLab's toolbox for generation and creation, used for text-to-image, image and video restoration, upscaling, and editing. Models and training scripts already have ready interfaces, and inpainting is only one of the tasks. If you want to try several generative models in the same library, you can switch among them here without installing a separate stack for each model.
vllm-project/vllm-omni: vLLM's multimodal inference framework for running image, audio, and video generation models efficiently. The focus is deployment and throughput, not a canvas or an editing interface. You can start a service on your own machine and let other programs call these models. It suits a backend that needs to serve several modalities at once.
GuanYixuan/pyJianYingDraft: A Python tool that generates Jianying drafts. You can place video, images, a timeline, and effects in code, then export the draft into Jianying and keep editing, which is a way to build an automatic editing pipeline. The CapCut version is developed in another repository. It suits people who need to produce videos in batches and still want drafts that can be edited again.
NVlabs/neuralangelo: NVIDIA's high-fidelity neural surface reconstruction, for recovering a detailed 3D surface from photos, with contours that fit the object more closely than earlier neural radiance fields. This is the official code from CVPR 2023. The output is a surface mesh, not a texture or a video. It suits reconstructing an object's shape from real footage.
dcajasn/Riskfolio-Lib: A Python library for portfolio optimization. You can compute the efficient frontier, risk, and weights, and compare different allocations. It is a research tool, not a program that automatically places orders with a broker. It suits asset allocation and risk analysis, and placing orders requires you to connect a trading interface separately.
vladmandic/sdnext: SD.Next is a local web interface for running diffusion models to generate and edit images, and it can also handle video and write descriptions. It supports many GPUs and CPUs, and the model can be swapped. It suits people who want a Stable Diffusion workbench that keeps being updated, rather than relying only on an older interface.
AbdBarho/stable-diffusion-webui-docker: An install package for running the Stable Diffusion web interface with Docker. You can open a ready-made interface and generate images without building a Python environment yourself. The repository itself is not a model. It packages an existing interface as a container. It suits people who want to run an image-generation service on their own machine quickly.
antgroup/echomimic_v2: Ant Group's half-body portrait animation, which uses audio to drive speech and body movement. You can give it an audio clip and a reference image, and it generates a video with matched lips and pose. CVPR 2025. The focus is portrait performance, not general video editing or text-to-video. It suits talking-head videos and virtual humans.
Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo-1.5: Tencent Hunyuan's lightweight video generation model, which can make a video from text or from an image. The focus is a small model that is easy to run while keeping a watchable picture. The official code and the notes on the weights are in this repository. It suits people who want to try text-to-video on their own machine without deploying an extremely large model first.
quantopian/alphalens: A Python library for judging how accurate a stock-selection factor is. You can look at how a signal relates to later returns, grouped returns, and turnover, and then decide whether it is worth taking into a backtest. It is a research tool, not an order-placing program. Quantopian has shut down, but the code can still be used for factor analysis.
civitai/civitai: Civitai's open-source program for running a community site that shares models, textual inversions, and LoRAs. You can browse, upload, and download weights trained by other people, rather than generating images from text here. It suits people who want to host a model-sharing site themselves, or see how the platform is built.
AbdullahAlfaraj/Auto-Photoshop-StableDif: A Photoshop plugin for calling Stable Diffusion directly inside Photoshop to generate and edit images. The backend can be Automatic1111, and it can also connect to ComfyUI. You stay with the original layers and tools, without exporting the image and pasting it back. The plugin itself is not a model.
tmoroney/auto-subs: A tool for making subtitles on your own computer, so the audio and video do not have to be uploaded. It can be used on its own, and it can also connect to DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, and After Effects. It supports multilingual transcription and translation, and it can tell who is speaking. It suits people who need local subtitles and want them to go straight into editing software.
shashankvemuri/Finance: A Python toolkit for quantitative research. You can pull market data, compute technical indicators, screen stocks, backtest strategies, and optimize a portfolio. The examples are a starting point, and you change the rules yourself. It is a research tool, not a program that automatically places orders with a broker. It suits people who want to try a strategy starting from the data.
zvtvz/zvt: A modular quantitative framework for pulling market data, building factors, and backtesting in one place. Stocks are the main subject, and it also covers cryptocurrency data. You can swap the data source and the strategy without writing a separate stack for each market. It suits people who want to study different markets with the same program. You have to connect trade execution yourself.
fudan-generative-vision/champ: Portrait animation guided by 3D parameters, which can turn one portrait into a stable video according to the motion. ECCV 2024. The focus is keeping the person's motion and appearance consistent, not general text-to-video. It suits research on character animation from a single photo. The official code follows the paper.
FlashML-org/FreeVideo: An inference engine for running MiniMax H3 video generation on a home computer, with VRAM that can be as low as 8GB. It chooses precision according to the GPU and loads the weights in batches, so the whole model does not have to sit in VRAM at once. The interface is a ComfyUI workspace, with launchers for Windows, Mac, and Linux as well. The model is an existing one, and this repository runs it locally.
wheresryan22/anatomy: A Claude skill for turning a concept into an interactive isometric mechanical diagram. The output is SVG, WebGL, or 3D, with the parts broken down finely. It asks a coding assistant to build an object you can understand, rather than only returning a passage of text. It can also be used in Codex and OpenCode.
rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner: A tool for turning off ads, hot-search prompts, and promotional notifications on Chinese-brand Android phones. It does not need root, and the changes can be undone. You can plug in the phone and click through a desktop program, or hand it to an AI agent to run all at once. It suits people who want to clear system ads without flashing the phone.
andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo: An agent skill that generates a digital-human talking-head video from one photo and one script. It calls Renoise's service for lip sync and packaging, rather than training a model from scratch on your machine. It suits people who want to hand the job to Claude Code or Codex to produce a talking-head video.
Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill: A set of Claude skills that scan charts, follow the news, and replay old price paths using free public data. Before you place an order, you can look back at how a pattern moved afterward. It is a research and review tool, not a broker order-placing program, and it does not guarantee that you will make money.
storytold/effectcraft: Open-source motion-graphics and compositing software written in Rust. You can build frames and effects on a timeline without relying on a subscription compositing tool. The program is written by the author, and it suits people who want a lightweight compositor. Compositing and editing a finished film are two different jobs.
Arekejoker/qwen21-nsfw-pose-skill: An agent skill for generating images from a pose with Qwen-Image inside ComfyUI. The recipe includes prompts, an adult-oriented LoRA, and more than a hundred 3D poses. It suits people who want a coding assistant to follow fixed steps and produce the images. The content is adult-oriented, not a general illustration tool.
patch-gg/anymove: It captures the motion of any creature from a video, fits that motion onto a skeleton, and exports GLB. The same frame has two camera views, used to align the joints. It can also be used as an agent skill and handed to a coding assistant to run. It suits games and 3D characters that need motion and do not have a motion-capture studio.
deepopen-com/deepopen-3d-webs: From one reference image and a prompt, it generates a previewable 3D scene along a camera path. The browser can play color, depth, and a Gaussian point cloud. The site is started with Docker. It suits people who want to go from one photo to a replayable scene, rather than ending with only a still image.
wide-trace/open-higgsfield: An open-source image and video studio that calls several existing models with one prompt. You have to bring your own platform keys. The studio itself is not a model. It suits people who want to try different image and video models on the same screen without being locked to a single website.
Gen-Verse/RSI-Anything: Research on using world models for recursive self-improvement. The system first predicts the next outcome, then learns from the interaction, and then changes the next decision. The repository follows the paper. It suits seeing how a world model takes part in a decision, not a game you can play right away.
kaomei/stickman-video-director: An open-source pipeline that turns a script or a topic into a stick-figure animation. Picture, voiceover, subtitles, and sound effects can be assembled in one pass. It suits faceless channels, without drawing every frame yourself. The output is a finished video, not only a storyboard. The finished video stays on your computer.
jundizhou/easy-stock: A desktop investment-research workbench for A-shares. You can watch quotes, research individual stocks, and review after the close, then ask an AI to organize the evidence. It is an analysis tool, not a program that automatically places orders with a broker. It suits people who want to do that review on their own machine. You make the judgment yourself.
scenario-labs/blender-plugin: Scenario's Blender add-on, which can generate images, video, 3D models, and PBR materials in the viewport. It also opens a local MCP so an agent can call these features. It requires Blender 5.0 or newer. Generation calls their service, and it is not a model built into Blender.
mylxsw/aidea: A mobile app written in Flutter that puts several large language models and image-generation models in one program. You can chat and also generate images, and the model interface can be swapped. The program is open source. It suits people who want to connect different models on a phone with their own keys.
t3dotgg/tstack: A collection of the agent skills Theo uses every day, cleaned up so other people can use them. They can run in Claude Code and Codex. When T3 Code is present they use its features, and when it is not they fall back to the native tools. It suits people who want a ready set of everyday development skills without writing skills from scratch.
DenisSergeevitch/ex-ussr-kinship-researc: A genealogy skill for AI agents, specifically for looking up kinship records from the former Soviet Union, the Soviet Union, and the Russian Empire. It reads church registers and civil, military, and exile archives, and it separates what is confirmed from what is inferred. It suits people who need to trace a family and want every item to keep its source.
lexmount/moli: A headless browser written in Rust for an AI agent to control web pages. The emphasis is that it is light, fast, and highly compatible. You can open pages and carry out actions in an environment with no window. It suits people who want their own agent to browse the web without relying on a heavy browser.
OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image: OpenMOSS's image model with 5 billion parameters, strong at text inside images and at layout. It can be fine-tuned. The official code and the notes on the weights are here. It suits image generation that needs clearly rendered text, not a canvas application. You have to download the model yourself and then run it.
obsidianmd/pele: Obsidian's official Mermaid diagram renderer, which turns diagrams into SVG. The program is small, runs synchronously, and has no runtime dependencies, and its colors follow CSS variables. It supports the diagram types in Mermaid 12. It suits producing a flowchart quickly, not doing video compositing.
openfilm/openfilm: An open-source AI video agent. You can turn the coding assistant you are already using into a video assistant, and after it finishes there is still an editor for changing the frames it generated. It suits people who want to build a video through conversation and then edit it section by section, rather than only receiving a finished piece. Generation and editing stay in the same workflow.
mexicat/pdoom-video: A music video rendered by a program, with subtitles timed to the song. Each frame is determined by the song's time, so the browser preview matches the exported 1080p or 4K. It is a work for this song, not a general video-making tool. You can render it again on your own machine.
Noniv/web-ocean: A WebGPU ocean-rendering demo. A single HTML file can open it in Chrome. It has FFT waves, foam, sunlight, and a sunset sky. You can fly the camera freely. There is no game engine. It suits looking at how a real-time water surface is written, not a 3D software package.
11cafe/jaaz: An open-source multimodal creation assistant that can run locally, for design and generation, positioned as an alternative to tools like Canva. Privacy comes first. It suits people who want to create images and text on their own machine without handing drafts to a subscription website. Drafts and conversations can both stay on the machine.
Picsart-AI-Research/Text2Video-Zero: It uses a text-to-image diffusion model to make video in a zero-shot way. Without training a new model for video, it can generate short clips from text or from an image. This is the official code for an ICCV 2023 oral. It suits research into how an image model can be extended to video.
lightly-ai/lightly: A Python self-supervised learning library for learning representations on images, and it also includes latent world models. You can train on unlabeled images and then use the representations for downstream tasks. It suits visual pretraining, not a video-making program or a trading program.
luigifreda/pyslam: Visual SLAM in a mix of Python and C++. It supports monocular, stereo, and RGB-D, can estimate how the camera moves, and also includes Gaussian splatting and semantic segmentation. It suits research on localization and reconstruction. It is a full pipeline, not only a point-cloud viewer.
xai-org/grok-build: SpaceXAI's terminal coding agent. The full-screen interface can view a project, edit files, and run commands. It can also run with no interface, or be embedded in an editor through the Agent Client Protocol. The program is written in Rust and is synced from their main repository. It suits handing development work to the terminal without opening a web chat window.
Jakeschincariol/replica-skill: Eleven Claude skills for taking apart an app's workflow and having an agent build one again. They require that only the functionality be rebuilt, without copying the code, the logo, or the copy. They can be installed as a plugin in Claude Code. It suits people who want to use a skill pack to try a similar product, not a ready-made application.
morganlinton/BeautifulRust: Rust skills for coding agents. One teaches idiomatic writing, one handles review and points out which rule applies, and one ports programs from C, Python, and other languages to Rust. There is also a clippy configuration that can be placed in CI. It suits people who want an agent to follow the official style when writing Rust, without pasting a guide themselves every time.
sirioberati/Genjustsu-Open-Source-Workfl: A local interface for replacing a person or an object in a video. It prepares depth, a SAM mask, and a face mesh, then hands them to Seedance to generate, and on export it keeps the original audio for the whole clip. You need to connect the Enhancor API separately. It suits character replacement, and it is not a video model trained by this project.
glanderness/BeefTV: A local-first AI video workbench that connects assets, models, and agents on a canvas. The desktop version can run on your own machine, from storyboard changes through to a finished film. Commercial use of the new code requires a separate license. It suits people who want to build a video on a canvas, and it is not a video model trained from scratch.
Vincentwei1021/anything2explainer: A Claude Code and Codex skill that uses Remotion to turn a topic into an explainer short, with voiceover, subtitles, and a chapter bar. Every frame is drawn by code, not by a generative model. Both Chinese and English work. The tool itself is under a non-commercial license. It suits using an agent to produce an explainer, rather than receiving a ready-made video.
yanliudesign/mono-color-skill: An image skill for producing monochrome or two-color editorial images, such as posters, zines, and portraits. The default is one main color plus a small accent, and the background can be white paper or warm paper. It is style guidance, not a new image model. It suits images with a printed look, not ordinary full-color generation.
hi3d-official/Hi3Dv1.0: Hi3D's official inference program. It uses a reference image to refine a coarse mesh into higher-resolution geometry. The base is Sparc3D, and the weights are on Hugging Face. The repository has inference and no training code. It suits adding detail to a coarse model you already have, not generating from scratch from a single image.
arnegiacomo/fugleramme: It uses a local sound model to recognize birds in the garden, then displays them as nineteenth-century hand-drawn illustrations. It can sit on e-paper, a television, or a Raspberry Pi. Recognition is done on your own machine. Whichever species is heard, that picture is swapped in. It suits setting up a bird picture frame, not video compositing or a 3D scene.
absolute-quantum/cats-blender-plugin: A Blender add-on for tidying models from MMD, Mixamo, DAZ, and similar sources, then sending them to VRChat. One click can reduce the polygon count, set up lip sync and eye tracking, and merge bones. It suits shortening the steps for uploading a virtual character, and it is not a render engine.
AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRL-Trading: Quantitative trading infrastructure in the FinRL series, called FinRL-X. It gathers data, strategies, backtesting, and broker order placement into one weight interface. There is a PyPI package and a paper. It suits people who want to go from researching a strategy to simulated order placement, rather than only a reinforcement-learning tutorial library.
simonlin1212/TradingAgents-astock: A multi-agent investment-research framework that adapts TradingAgents for A-shares. Seven analysts debate using data such as the dragon-tiger list and lock-up expirations. It can be installed with pip, and it is positioned as research and teaching. It suits trying multi-role investment research, not an automatic order-placing trading program.
airbnb/lottie-web: Airbnb's web Lottie player renders JSON exported from After Effects through Bodymovin. It only plays the animation in a browser. The motion is authored in AE or another tool, then exported.
airbnb/lottie-android: Airbnb's Android Lottie player renders animations exported from After Effects through Bodymovin. It is a native playback component, so the file is authored in AE or another tool first.
airbnb/lottie-ios: Airbnb's iOS Lottie player renders vector animations exported from After Effects on iPhone and iPad. It is a playback component, so the motion is authored in AE and then exported.
Tencent/libpag: Tencent's PAG renderer turns After Effects animations into a portable file and plays them on mobile, web, and desktop. PAG and Lottie JSON are different formats. It is a player, not a full editor or compositor.
LottieFiles/dotlottie-web: LottieFiles' dotLottie web player uses Rust and WebAssembly to play compressed Lottie files. It plays After Effects exports in the browser. It is a player, not a timeline editor.
lottie-react-native/lottie-react-native: A React Native wrapper around the native Lottie players, used to play After Effects exports inside an app. It is a framework binding, so the animation is still authored in AE.
Samsung/rlottie: Samsung's standalone C++ library plays Lottie JSON exported from After Effects through Bodymovin, without a browser. It is a playback engine, not an editor or compositor.
alyssaxuu/motionity: A timeline motion-graphics editor that runs in the browser, for cutting animation, type, images, and effects, then exporting a clip. It is an editor, not a node compositor. After Effects is not required; a browser is enough.
tixl3d/tixl: TiXL is a desktop app for realtime motion graphics, built with nodes and a timeline. Parameter changes show up immediately. It is a standalone program, not an After Effects plugin.
mojs/mojs: A motion-graphics toolbelt for the web. Code draws shapes, tweens, timelines, and burst effects in the browser. The motion is written in code, without opening AE. It is a front-end library, not an After Effects plugin or a video editor.
astrofox-io/astrofox: Astrofox is a motion-graphics program that turns an audio track into visuals that follow the beat and the spectrum, then exports a clip. It is built for music visualization, not general editing or compositing, and it does not need After Effects.
motion-canvas/motion-canvas: A framework for motion graphics written in TypeScript. You lay out a timeline and tweens in code, then render a video. It is code-driven motion, not an After Effects plugin, and AE is not required.
theatre-js/theatre: A motion-design editor for the web. You adjust animation on a visual timeline and hand it to front-end code to play. It is a motion-design tool, not After Effects or a video editor, and AE is not required.
rezoo/movis: A Python library for video, motion graphics, and shader art. You stack layers and render from code. It is a library, not an After Effects plugin, and the machine does not need AE.
ManimCommunity/manim: The community Python framework for mathematical animation. It draws formulas and geometry step by step and renders a teaching film. It makes teaching videos, not commercial After Effects comps, and AE is not required.
inlife/nexrender: Data-driven render automation for After Effects. It swaps text and footage in batches and outputs the renders. After Effects must be installed on the machine, because nexrender asks AE to render.
RxLaboratory/Duik: Duik Ángela is a rigging and character-animation tool that runs inside After Effects, adding skeletons and controllers to layers. It is an AE panel, not a standalone 3D app, so After Effects must be installed.
ntsc-rs/ntsc-rs: A Rust VHS and analog-TV look. It runs as a standalone app and also as a plugin for After Effects, Premiere, and OpenFX. It is an effect, not a full compositor.
baku89/ISF4AE: An After Effects plugin that runs GLSL written as ISF, so a custom shader becomes an effect inside AE. It is a plugin, not a transition pack, and After Effects must be installed.
JacquesLucke/animation_nodes: A Blender add-on that builds motion graphics with nodes, driving objects, time, and effects procedurally. It runs in Blender, not as an After Effects plugin, so AE is not required.
toadstorm/MOPS: Motion Operators for Houdini, a node toolkit for motion graphics and procedural animation. It runs in Houdini, not on After Effects layers, and the machine does not need AE.
mrachinskiy/commotion: A Blender add-on for motion graphics, used to build procedural animation and effects inside Blender. It is not an After Effects plugin, and After Effects does not need to be installed.
xvrh/lottie-flutter: A pure-Dart Flutter player for Lottie animations exported from After Effects. It is a playback widget, not a video editor, so the animation is authored in AE and then exported.
thorvg/thorvg: A production C++ vector engine that renders SVG and Lottie, meant to be embedded in other programs. It is a graphics library, not After Effects and not a video editor, and AE is not required.
valentderah/totk-pc-recomp: A static recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom into a Windows program with a Vulkan renderer. Game files are not in the repo; you need your own legal copy. It is a game port, not a Blender or compositing tool, and it is still early.
Leonxlnx/earshot: Ears for coding agents: describe a sound, synthesize it in code, then listen and revise. It runs on CPU and includes an MCP server. It is for UI sounds and score, not a video editor or a newly trained music model.
onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent: A roughly seven-dollar ESP32 lets an existing vision model use a real iPhone: AirPlay for eyes and USB HID for hands. No Mac, developer account, or jailbreak. It is a hardware bridge, not a newly trained model.
zai-org/ZCode: Z.ai's coding workbench, with desktop, browser, and terminal agents. The repo includes the client, backend, and agent runtime. It is a coding harness, not an image or video model.
Tejashmakwana/motionmaxxing: An agent skill for motion graphics. It renders with Chrome and ffmpeg and tries to make AI videos look like a motion designer's work. It is a skill plus a render path, not an After Effects plugin.
QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1: Qwen's released image model, about 7B parameters in the visual part. It does text-to-image, editing, transparent images, and up to ten reference images. Weights and code are included, under a research license for research and evaluation only; commercial use needs a separate license.
langchain-ai/design-agent: LangChain's open design agent. From a chat it makes on-brand stills, decks, charts, and motion graphics, built on Deep Agents. It is not After Effects; the files come from the agent and the model.
StreamEval/StreamEval: A benchmark and dataset for evaluating interactive streaming video-generation models, with a paper, a test set, and Hugging Face data. It measures realtime interaction. It does not generate the videos itself, and it is not a video editor.
ChatAnyTeam/ChatAny: An unmaintained web app based on ChatGPT-Next-Web. It connects ChatGPT and several AI services, including image tools. It is an aggregator interface, not an image model, and the author says this project is no longer maintained.
GVCLab/PersonaLive: A CVPR 2026 portrait-animation model from the paper authors. One photo becomes an expressive face meant for a live stream, driven by a motion signal. It is their research code, not a general video editor or a wrapped streaming app.
junyanz/iGAN: Berkeley's 2016 interactive image generator. Sketches and brush strokes drive a GAN in real time. It is that era's Torch research code, not a Blender plugin or a modern diffusion model.
edtechre/pybroker: A Python library for algorithmic-trading backtests, including machine-learning signals. The license is Apache 2.0 plus the Commons Clause, so you cannot sell the library itself. It backtests; it is not a broker order tool.
tradytics/eiten: Tradytics' portfolio toolkit. It builds stock portfolios with eigen portfolios, minimum variance, maximum Sharpe, and genetic algorithms, and you can pick the stocks and test them. It is for research and allocation, not live broker orders.
Louis-CFM/coucou: A small companion in the Mac notch, and on Windows, Linux, and phones, that watches coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. You can approve permissions and drop files. It is a monitor, not an agent that writes the code.
google/artemis: Google's Android automation tool. AI assistants and test suites can use a real phone like a person, run a full workflow, and capture logs. It automates phones, not a general coding agent.
CopilotKit/OpenDuet: CopilotKit's template for a proactive agent, built on OpenBot, that does the work and checks back so you can step in. It is still early. It is a starter template, not a separately trained model.
D3voz/openjutsu: A local one-click character-swap app. The Next.js front end runs a ComfyUI workflow on existing MiniMax H3, SAM, and Qwen3-VL weights. It is a wrapper app, not a newly trained video model.
cclank/lanshu-create-ai-presenter-video: A Codex skill for presenter videos. It takes a script and an authorized presenter image, then renders with HyperFrames. It is a skill that calls existing services, not a newly trained digital-human model.
Tencent-Hunyuan/Prism: Tencent Hunyuan's research model for joint video and audio generation, using dynamic sparse attention and aiming at 2K. Weights are on Hugging Face. It is the paper's model, not an image editor or a video editor.
EL4CTEO/blender-skills: Twenty-two Blender 5.2 agent skills for modeling, UVs, materials, rigging, animation, rendering, and checks, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others. It is a skill pack, and Blender must be installed.
EverettFish/holo-card-studio: A Codex skill for holographic cards. One description or reference image becomes an editable Blender card and a Three.js page. It is a skill, not a standalone 3D application.
blixvip/NullMotion: Plays a finished motion-graphics ad in sync with the HyperFrames drafts it grew from, then exports that breakdown as an MP4. It is a breakdown player, not After Effects or an editor you start from scratch.
veedstudio/open-edit: An editing pipeline for coding agents. A text description can add subtitles, motion graphics, and slides, then render an MP4. It is an agent editing pipeline, not After Effects.
yl4579/StyleTTS2: A research text-to-speech model that uses style diffusion to pick a voice without a reference recording. It synthesizes speech, not images, even though its topics mention diffusion.
imbue-bit/AlphaGPT: A research program that searches for quantitative factors with deep reinforcement learning. The repo has a data pipeline, model core, and strategy manager, and you connect your own data. Check the results yourself. It is a factor-research tool, not a broker, and it does not guarantee profit.
LLMQuant/quant-mind: A knowledge extraction and retrieval framework for quantitative finance. It is a Python package an agent can use to build and query financial material for later research. It is a data tool, not a backtester or an order-placing program.
alsk1992/CloddsBot: A trading terminal for crypto, futures, and prediction markets. An AI agent can scan markets and place orders across exchanges and prediction markets. Review the risk before an order. It is trading software, not a strategy that guarantees profit, and losses are yours.
alchaincyf/huashu-motion: A product-film skill for coding agents. It can compose music and you can point at a frame to change it. The film is rendered from code. It is a skill, not After Effects or a newly trained video model.
QingYunA/answer-me-with-html: An agent skill that answers a hard question with one readable HTML page, including figures, tables, and flows, instead of a long block of plain text. It is an answer format, not a browser or a newly trained model.
kaankiziltug/logo-design-skill: A logo-design skill for Claude, Codex, and Gemini, with principles, a process, SVG craft, and test tools, plus a library of about 1,400 reference logos. It is a skill, not a design app that draws logos by itself.
DozenTwelve/Papermorph: A skill that turns a book into an interactive web page with animation and narration. The agent lays out the frames, and narration can use an existing voice. It is a skill, not a video editor. You need the right to use the book.
HeyChengC/wallstreet-explainer: A skill for spare, finance-explainer shorts. It sets the look, finds footage, takes stills, adds voice, and renders, with numbers shown as simple charts. The sample's live footage and news images are credited sources. It is a skill, not a newly trained video model.
sixtysevenlf/dsh-blender-plugin: A plugin that connects DeepSeek Harness to Blender. An agent can change, check, and export a scene in an open Blender, or run the same loop headless. Blender must be installed, and a modeling skill is included.
alexgreensh/anidoodle: A tool for illustrations, loops, and scored films drawn in code. Every frame and sound effect is drawn by the program, and an agent skill can ask it to render. It is not After Effects or a hand-drawing app.
ChenYilong/CYLTabBarController: An iOS tab-bar library. It animates tab icons with Lottie and Liquid Glass, and can add a larger center button and a badge. It is an app UI component, not a video editor or After Effects.
bytedance/LatentSync: ByteDance's lip-sync research. A diffusion model moves the mouth to match audio, for avatars and dubbed speech. Weights are on Hugging Face. It is a lip-sync model, not an image editor or a general video editor.
hello245m/free-stockdb: A local data engine for China A-shares and ETFs. It incrementally syncs daily and minute bars, adjusts prices, computes indicators, and backtests. Data stays on your machine. It is a research store, not a broker.
letianzj/QuantResearch: Quantitative research notebooks and backtest examples. Jupyter covers portfolio optimization, machine learning, and deep-reinforcement-learning strategies. The strategies are demonstrations, not a live order system, and you should check the examples yourself.
Humpalumps/Ultra-Water: A real-time ocean renderer for three.js. FFT drives shore breakers, foam, caustics, and buoyancy, aiming at a high frame rate in the browser. It is a web water surface, not a Blender fluid sim, and it has been public for less than a day, so the look can still change.
Vincentwei1021/video-shotcraft: A video skill for Claude Code and Codex. It builds editable product promos in Remotion, with shot cards, motion previews, and a JianYing export. It is a skill, not a newly trained video model.
udhaykumarbala/cleanyourtv-app: An Android phone app that clears ads and preinstalled items from an Android TV or Fire TV, without a computer. It is listed under AI Agent because the description mentions the word agent. It is not an AI agent, and it says it does not uninstall the system.
daveebbelaar/bama: Agent skills for Mac apps. They take a Swift and SwiftUI app from an idea to the Dock, and can study an existing app so you rebuild your own. You do not open the Xcode interface. It is a skill, and you compile the result.
HeyChengC/vibe-knowledge-film: A skill for the look of viral knowledge shorts. It studies a reference, builds a shot list, adds sound, and renders. The look imitates the reference. It is not a newly trained video model, the sample does not give you the original film, and you should watch the result.
eternityspring/reelbench-skills: Video skills for Claude Code and Codex, including shot analysis and ffmpeg tools. The README also treats the repo as learning notes. It is a skill pack, not a newly trained video model.
howseen-ai/claude-motion-design: A Claude Code skill for motion design. It renders films from HTML with Playwright and ffmpeg. After Effects is not required, and neither is a Remotion license. It is a skill, not a video editor.
op7418/guizang-ppt-skill: An agent skill for slide decks. It builds magazine or Swiss-style HTML slides, with image prompts and social covers. It is a skill, not PowerPoint and not an image model. The license is AGPL.
wiltodelta/remove-ai-watermarks: A Python library, command-line tool, and agent skill that clears visible marks and provenance metadata such as C2PA and EXIF from images and video you generated. Stripping those marks does not turn a generated image into a photograph.
DLR-RM/BlenderProc: A Blender pipeline from the German Aerospace Center. It procedurally renders photorealistic training images and can control the scene and camera. Blender must be installed. The output is synthetic training data, not a finished film composite.
marketcalls/openalgo: An open algorithmic-trading platform. It connects brokers, charts, and strategies written in Python, and it includes a trading interface. It is a Python service for orders and research, not a bot that guarantees profit. The license is AGPL.
brndnmtthws/thetagang: An options bot for Interactive Brokers that runs theta-style strategies. It is listed under crypto, but it trades stock options, not exchange spot crypto. It does not guarantee a profit, and losses are yours.
wquguru/nof0: An open reproduction of the NOF1 trading arena, for comparing LLM agents as they trade on Hyperliquid. Arena results are not the same as live trading. It is a comparison environment, not a strategy that has been shown to profit.
google/elephant-goldfish-model: Google's skills for designing and reviewing software. The name says model, but the repo is a skill pack for Claude Code, Codex, and similar agents. You install it into a coding agent. It is not a newly trained language model.
trycompai/crm: An open CRM designed so AI agents can record customers and follow-ups, including sales, records, and the next step. It is CRM software, not an assistant that runs a business by itself.
Human-Agent-Society/reef: Infrastructure for agents that keep improving. The repo covers inference, training, and reinforcement learning for agents that run for a long time. It is a foundation, not a finished assistant you can open and use, and it is still research infrastructure.
jd-opensource/JoyAI-Video-Edit: JD's open real-time video-editing model. Autoregressive diffusion makes open-ended changes from text. Weights are on Hugging Face. It is an editing model, not a timeline editor, and you should watch the result.
MisakaZentai/world-execute-me-dsh-pv: A code-rendered fan PV for one song, shown as a TUI and a chat window. The code is MIT and the artwork is CC BY-NC-SA, so the pictures are not commercial stock. The song title is the subject. It is one film, not a VFX tool.
sitor-ai/frametell: A local-first director agent for explainer videos. It can use whatever model you already have, arrange your ideas and material, and render on your machine. It is a directing flow, not a newly trained video model. The license is AGPL, and you need the right to use the material.
MengTo/kage: An interactive five-chapter night walk through a Kyoto mountain temple. Three.js moves a live camera through the scene and layers generated imagery on top. It runs in the browser. It is one artwork, not a Blender or compositing tool, and the temple walk is fictional.
op7418/guizang-product-video-skill: A product-video skill for Claude Code and Codex. It reuses real product components and design language to make an update film in code, with a shot list, music, and a render. It is a skill, not a newly trained video model. The license is AGPL.
Akegarasu/lora-scripts: Scripts and a graphical interface around the kohya-ss trainer for LoRA and DreamBooth fine-tuning of diffusion models. You bring your own dataset. It is a training tool, not a new model. The license is AGPL.
Fanghua-Yu/SUPIR: CVPR 2024 photo-restoration research. A diffusion model tries to make damaged real-world photos look clearer. There is a paper and an online demo. The license is SupPixel's own terms, so commercial use has extra conditions. It is not a standard open-source grant.
open-gigaai/giga-brain-0: A vision-language-action model for robots, built on a world model, aiming at emergent manipulation skills. The repo publishes the code and the weight notes. It is an embodied model, not a video world you walk around in.
exchange-core/exchange-core: A Java matching engine aimed at crypto, forex, and high-frequency exchanges. It can sit in an exchange backend. It matches orders. It is not a trading strategy, it does not guarantee profit, and high frequency is a design goal you have to measure yourself.
LottieFiles/motion-design-skill: A LottieFiles skill that gives AI agents motion-design principles: timing, easing, choreography, and Disney-style animation rules. It is a principles pack, not a Lottie player and not After Effects.
wangzan101/Mika: A private assistant on Android. You give it one sentence, and it operates apps you already installed and web pages on a background screen. You bring the model, through an API or a local server. It is not a newly trained model. It is a public beta. The license is Apache-2.0.
ccch1mneyyy/dsh-Go: An unofficial Android client for DeepSeek Harness. The phone can run it in a local Linux environment, or connect to DSH on your own computer. Model requests still go to the provider you configure. It is not affiliated with DeepSeek. The app license is AGPL-3.0, and the mascots are outside that license.
genspark-ai/genoffice: An open office suite that opens and saves real docx, xlsx, and pptx files, and can edit PDFs. A built-in agent edits the document, and a CLI plus a skill let Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor do that locally. You bring your own API key. It is not a new model. The license is Apache-2.0.
5hyuns/maya-workflow-kit-for-blender: A free Blender extension that brings Maya habits into Blender: a hotbox, marking menus, a Channel Box, and an attribute editor. You need Blender. It is a Blender extension, not Autodesk Maya. The license is GPL-3.0.
v-modal/vmodal_sdk_flutter: A Flutter SDK for searching video by picture, speech, and on-screen text. Uploads and indexing go through VModal's service, and you need your own API key. It is a client SDK, not a video model that runs on your machine. The license is MIT.
noahdunnagan/mcopt: A Fabric mod for Minecraft Java Edition. On Apple Silicon Macs it draws the world with its own Metal renderer. It is still alpha, so back up your worlds. It is a game renderer, not a Blender or compositing tool. The license is Apache-2.0.
Nyankomintsu/world-execute-me-lyric-mv: A fan lyric video for one song, drawn frame by frame in code, as a chat window and print-style pictures. The repo has no song and no lyrics; you need the right to add both. It is one film, not a VFX tool. The code license is MIT.
liyupi/ai-promo-video-maker: A product-video skill for Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex. It builds the film from a Remotion template and scripts. Voiceover can use ElevenLabs; without a key it uses captions. It is a skill, not a newly trained video model. The license is MIT. Larger companies need a separate Remotion license.
shy3130/tick-stock-panel: A self-hosted A-share research workbench for writing strategies, monitoring, and backtests. You can plug in your own data. The author says it is not investment software and it does not recommend stocks. It is a research bench, not a broker. The license is MIT, for research.
ATH-MaaS/ComfyUI-Copilot: A smart node inside ComfyUI that can inspect a workflow, debug it, and change nodes from a description. The vendor API is suspended, so you fill in your own API key and address. It is an assistant node, not a new image model and not a workflow collection. The license is MIT.
man-group/ArcticDB: A serverless database for Pandas tables, stored on S3 or LMDB, suited to time series. Research use is available. Production use, or offering it as a database service, needs a paid license. It is a database, not a trading strategy. GitHub does not mark a standard open-source license.
TNT-Likely/PanWatch: A self-hosted stock monitor for A-shares, Hong Kong, and US stocks. It uses the existing TradingAgents project for analysis, holdings, and alerts, and it includes paper trading. It is a monitor, not an exchange, and it does not guarantee profit. The license is MIT.
Lumiwealth/lumibot: A Python trading framework for backtests, paper trading, and live orders across stocks, options, futures, forex, crypto, and prediction markets. A strategy uses your own model and broker. It is a framework, not a strategy that earns money. The license is GPL-3.0.
XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt: Use the ChatGPT website you already pay for as the planner and reviewer, while Codex edits the code. The bridge is the official site plus a read-only MCP, and the whole repo is not uploaded. It is a bridge, not a reverse proxy and not a new model. The license is MIT.
CopilotKit/OpenBot: Each coworker agent gets its own browser, files, and tools. An action is decided first and recorded after. You bring any AG-UI agent and run it on your own machine. It is still beta. It is a coworker shell, not a newly trained model. The license is MIT.
cranebeaker/coop-anything: A skill pack and MCP so a coding agent can study a single-player game you already have and try to add online or split-screen co-op. It is skills and a process, not a finished multiplayer patch. You need the game. The license is MIT.
vincentsch/explainroo: An explainer-video skill for an AI agent. Speech uses the existing Kokoro model, word timing uses Whisper, and a canvas on your machine renders the MP4. It is a local flow, not a newly trained video model. The license is MIT.
viettranx/3dviz-pro-max: A 3D visualization skill for Claude Code and Codex. It turns an idea into a Three.js or Blender scene, with recipes and runnable examples. Your agent still has to build the picture. It is a skill pack, not a renderer you open and use. The license is MIT.
ng-native/ng-native: It draws Angular apps as real native iOS and Android views, using React Native's Fabric renderer. You need both frameworks. It is a mobile interface framework, not a Blender or effects tool. The license is MIT.
ant-research/4DAnyone: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 research. A casual single-camera video becomes consistent multi-view video for a later 4D Gaussian reconstruction. Weights download on first use, and you need a GPU. It is a generative model, not an editor. The code license is Apache-2.0.
WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame: An open game studio for one person. You make games on a canvas with your own model key, and it talks to many model providers. It is a game-making app, not a video model, and it does not guarantee you earn money. The license is Apache-2.0.
transformerlab/transformerlab-app: A training and evaluation environment for researchers, from a local machine to a GPU cluster, covering language models and diffusion models. You bring the data and the hardware. It is a research bench, not a new image model. The license is AGPL-3.0.
philz1337x/clarity-upscaler: A local image upscaler and enhancer built on a Stable Diffusion web interface. It uses an existing model and LoRAs to make a picture clearer. You run it yourself. It is an upscaling flow, not a newly trained base model. The license is AGPL-3.0.
skfolio/skfolio: A portfolio library on scikit-learn for allocation, factor models, and risk, and it can backtest. It is a research library, not a broker, and it does not guarantee profit. The license is BSD-3-Clause.
anandanand84/technicalindicators: Technical indicators and candlestick patterns written in TypeScript and calculated in the browser. You pass in prices and it returns numbers. It is an indicator library, not order software and not a strategy. The license is MIT. The last update was years ago.
vybenetwork/solana-swap-api: A demo of Vybe's hosted swap API: it fetches quotes and builds unsigned Solana transactions. You need your own API key. It is a demo client, not a router you run yourself. GitHub does not mark a license.
Thinklab-SJTU/Bench2Drive: A NeurIPS 2024 closed-loop driving benchmark. A world-model reinforcement-learning expert supplies the reference, and you compare driving models. It is a benchmark, not a world you play. The license is CC BY-NC-ND, so commercial use and redistributing changes are not allowed.
omnirush-ai/omnirush-gui: A desktop coding agent. Models come from the catalog on your omnirush.ai account, and your own provider keys are not supported. You can add skills and local MCP servers. It is a client, not a model you trained. The desktop app is MIT, and the ee directory has a separate license.
zhuyansen/new-term-radar: A daily radar and agent skill. It watches X, Hugging Face, GitHub, and sitemaps for names of new models and products, then writes a daily report. It is a monitor, not a new model. The license is MIT.
Oldcircle/geo-sleuth: An agent skill that estimates where a photo was taken, using street view, satellite tiles, elevation, and OpenStreetMap, and it shows how it narrowed the search. You install it in a coding agent. It is a skill, not a newly trained vision model. The license is MIT.
gatewai-dev/framefields: A library for compositing, motion graphics, and 3D on WebGPU. An agent drives it with code to make a picture. It is still beta. It is a render library, not After Effects and not a new video model. The license is Apache-2.0.
nikopueringer/CorridorKey2.0: A green-screen and blue-screen keying model. It needs an NVIDIA GPU, and the weights are about 5 GB downloaded separately. The license is a variation of CC BY-NC-SA, so integrating it into commercial software has extra terms. It is a keying model, not a Blender plugin.
snuri00/psp-web-recomp: It translates a PSP game you already own into WebAssembly and runs it in the browser. The repository does not include game files. It is a game recompiler and a WebGL renderer, not a Blender or effects tool. The license is MIT.
chipfighter/context-attachment-manager: A plugin for Codex and Claude. It lifts images out of the chat and fetches one back only when the model needs it, so a long conversation stays lighter. It manages attachments. It is not an image-generation model, and it does not draw a new picture. The license is MIT.
NikoDemon80/ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context: A ComfyUI node. It passes the last frames and audio of one MiniMax H3 clip into the next, so motion and sound can continue. You need ComfyUI and H3 already. It is a join node, not a new video model. The license is GPL-3.0.
pkuliyi2015/multidiffusion-upscaler-for-: An Automatic1111 extension. Tiled diffusion draws large images on a small graphics card, on top of an existing Stable Diffusion model. The license is CC BY-NC-SA, so you cannot sell this code. Pictures you make are not under that restriction.
ali-vilab/VACE: ICCV 2025 research for creating and editing video from text and other conditions. Weights are on Hugging Face. It is a model, not a timeline editor. The code license is Apache-2.0.
rorysroes/SGX-Full-OrderBook-Tick-Data-T: A notebook that studies a high-frequency order book with machine learning and shows how one simple strategy's profit and loss was counted. There is no license file. It is research notes, not a live trading program, and you have to recheck the result. The last update was years ago, and the data is not in the repo. For reference only.
barter-rs/barter-rs: A Rust trading framework for live trading, paper trading, and backtests. You plug in your own strategy and risk checks, across more than one market. It is a framework, not a strategy that earns money. You connect the exchange yourself before any order. The license is MIT. Measure the latency yourself.
Yvictor/TradingGym: A practice environment for reinforcement-learning trading. It supports tick data and candlesticks, for training and backtests. You bring the data. It is a gym, not a broker, and it does not place live orders by itself. The license is MIT. The last update was a while ago.
ccxt/go-binance: A Go client for the Binance API, with REST and websockets. You need your own account and key. It is an exchange SDK, not a trading strategy. The license is MIT.
microsoft/TokenEconomizer: Microsoft research that controls a coding agent's token spend from outside the black box, using past experience. You bring your own agent. It is cost control, not a newly trained agent. The license is Apache-2.0.
milind-soni/OpenMausBot: An open chat shell. Each bot in the sidebar is Claude or Codex running on your machine, plus a cloud computer. It is independent of Grok Bot and Meta Muse. It is a shell, not a new model. The license is Apache-2.0.
trhhubsd/ARTEX: A multi-agent research system for penetration testing, meant for an isolated lab, with a person confirming actions. It is a research system, not a finished tool you point at someone else's network. The license is AGPL-3.0. Read the lab scope before use.
Jetsku/KytyPS5: An experimental PS5 emulator fork with merged renderer and shader fixes. It does not claim a stable 60 frames per second. You supply the game. It is an emulator, not a Blender or effects tool. The license is GPL-2.0.
ahujasid/camera-to-blender: Take a phone photo, send it through the existing Tripo3D service to make a model, and paste that into Blender. You need an API key, and Blender has to be open. It is a bridge, not a newly trained 3D model. The license is MIT.
JimLiu/baocut: A local-first video agent with a timeline you can edit again. It can transcribe, subtitle, translate, dub, and cut, using existing local models or an online API. The source is usable, but selling the program itself needs a separate written license. It is an editing agent, not a new video model.
charlie947/motion-graphics-skills: Fifteen Claude Code skills that draw every frame in code for launch-grade motion graphics and an MP4. There is no After Effects and no video-generation model. You install them in a coding agent. The license is MIT.
ammaarreshi/Generals-Mac-iOS-iPad: It compiles the Command and Conquer Generals: Zero Hour engine for Mac, iPhone, and iPad, and renders with Metal. The repo has no game assets; you need your own legitimate copy. It is a game port, not Blender. The source follows EA's GPL v3 release.
Stability-AI/StableSwarmUI: A modular web interface for Stable Diffusion, for using existing models and extensions. Stability no longer maintains this repo; the independent continuation is SwarmUI. It is an interface, not a new model. The license is MIT.
OpenGVLab/DragGAN: An unofficial recreation of DragGAN. You drag points to change pose and shape on a GAN image. You run it yourself, and the model weights are separate. GitHub does not mark a license. It is an editing demo, not a newly trained base model. The last update was years ago.
thu-ml/SageAttention: A CUDA library for quantized attention. Inference can be faster than FlashAttention, and it plugs into language, image, and video models. It is a speed kernel, not a video model, and it does not change the model's scores. The license is Apache-2.0.
achillesrasquinha/bulbea: A Python library that uses deep learning to model and predict stocks from historical prices. The last update was years ago, so the interface may be stale. It is a prediction library, not a broker, and it does not guarantee accuracy. The license is Apache-2.0. For research.
asavinov/intelligent-trading-bot: An experiment that uses machine learning and feature engineering to emit signals and then trade crypto. You connect the data and the exchange yourself. It is an experiment, it does not guarantee profit, and you recheck any backtest. The license is MIT. A signal is not an order.
feitangyuan/onetake: A Claude agent skill for product films that never cut to the next slide. Each beat grows out of the one before, and an oracle measures continuity. It is a skill, not a new video model. The license is PolyForm Noncommercial, so only noncommercial use is allowed.
TencentCloud/Octop: Tencent Cloud's self-hosted assistant, with multiple users and agents, and files stay on your machine. You connect the chat model yourself. It does not include a new chat model. The local download is only an embedding model. The license is MIT. It is an assistant shell.
Jakeschincariol/founder-skill: Eleven Claude skills that test a business before launch: a board, marketing, pricing, and a buyer panel. No API key is required. The board is a prompt framework, not real people. It is a skill pack, and it does not guarantee profit. The license is MIT.
bangtutorial/bang-motion: A browser motion-graphics skill. One index.html makes openers, promos, and kinetic type for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. It is a skill, not After Effects and not a video model. The license is MIT.
mfranzon/print3d: A 3D-printing skill for a coding agent. Text or a photo becomes a Bambu Lab slice project. It targets the X2D or P2S with a 0.4 mm nozzle. It is a skill, not a newly trained 3D model. The license is MIT.
AlibabaResearch/SparkDiffusion: A framework that accelerates DiT video generation. The authors claim inference can be 265 times faster, using sparsity, distillation, and quantization. Weights are on Hugging Face. It is an accelerator, not a new video model, and you measure the speed yourself. The license is Apache-2.0.
arjun988/blender-skills: Ninety-four Blender skills for Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex. Through MCP they go from a blockout to an export. Blender has to be open. This pack is by a different author from the other blender-skills repo. It is a skill pack. The license is MIT.
anteloc/ldraw-nova: Tools so an agent can build LEGO and write an editable LDraw file. You install the parts library and LeoCAD yourself. Generation uses an existing coding agent. It is a tool, not a new model. The license is AGPL-3.0.
hao-ai-lab/FastVideo: An inference and post-training framework for video generation, including a fast checkpoint distilled from MiniMax H3. You need a GPU. It is a framework, not an editor and not an image editor. The license is Apache-2.0. Measure the speed yourself.
yangjian102621/geekai: A self-hosted creation console. It connects to existing services such as ChatGPT, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion for chat, pictures, and video. You bring your own accounts. It is an interface, not a new model. The license is Apache-2.0.
thu-ml/TurboDiffusion: A video-diffusion accelerator. It uses SageAttention and related kernels. The paper says 100 to 200 times faster. The checkpoints are not final, and long English prompts work better. It is an accelerator, not a new video model. The license is Apache-2.0.
coding-kitties/investing-algorithm-frame: A quantitative trading framework for writing strategies, large backtests, and deployment. You decide which one goes live, and you connect the market yourself. It is a framework, not a strategy that earns money. The license is Apache-2.0. Measure slippage yourself.
jmfernandes/robin_stocks: An unofficial Python library for the Robinhood, Gemini, and TD Ameritrade APIs. It can read quotes and place orders. You need your own account. It is an API library, not a broker, and it does not guarantee profit. The license is MIT.
