iart-ai/motion-skills: Fifty-six agent skills in nineteen packs. They teach a coding agent to make motion graphics, animation, and short video. You render with the agent you already use. It is a skill pack, not After Effects and not a new video model. The license is MIT.
lizhe00/AnimatableGaussians: Research code. Video is used to learn an animatable human body, with pose mapped to 3D Gaussians. It was presented at CVPR 2024. The Tsinghua license allows only non-commercial research, education, and art, and commercial use needs a separate grant. It has had few updates since November 2024. It is an avatar model, not a viewer.
THU-LYJ-Lab/T3Bench: A text-to-3D benchmark with three hundred prompts. Existing methods produce the results, which are then scored for quality and alignment. It has had few updates since October 2023. The repository includes no open-source license file. It is a benchmark, not a new 3D generator.
Pan-Chera/Multi-Agent-CAD: A multi-agent framework. A design brief becomes editable CAD, exported as STEP, STL, or GLB. Assembly generation is still experimental, so check it before you manufacture. It needs Python 3.11 or newer. It generates CAD, not a mesh from a photo. The license is MIT.
microsoft/skill-recorder: A desktop app. It records one task you do on your screen, then GitHub Copilot CLI turns that into an intent and ordered steps. A SKILL.md or a scheduled automation is saved only after you approve it. You need Copilot. It is a recorder, not a new model. The license is MIT.
JetBrains/thinkrail: A lightweight IDE from the JetBrains incubator, built around the pi coding agent. Work is isolated in git worktrees. It can remember a project and reuse skills, but it is an IDE, not a new model. The license is Apache-2.0.
Jakeschincariol/linkedin-agent-skill: Eleven Claude skills. They draft LinkedIn posts, comments, replies, a profile score, and a weekly plan. Nothing is posted until you agree. The humanizer only rewrites template-sounding copy. It is a skill pack, not LinkedIn and not a new model. The license is MIT.
3DTopia/3DTopia-XL: A research model. One image or a text prompt becomes a 3D asset with PBR materials. It was a CVPR 2025 highlight. Weights are on Hugging Face as FrozenBurning/3DTopia-XL. It is different from LGM and OpenLRM already in the catalog. It has had few updates since July 2025. The license is Apache-2.0.
Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab: A local pipeline. Existing models turn a prompt or one picture into a textured, rigged game character. It runs on Apple Silicon or NVIDIA. Check the license of each model yourself. It is a pipeline, not a new model. The license of this repository is Apache-2.0.
ed-asriyan/lottie-converter: A converter. It turns Lottie JSON, .lottie files, and Telegram TGS stickers into GIF, PNG, APNG, WEBP, or WEBM. You supply the source file. It is a converter, not After Effects. The license is MIT.
margelo/react-native-skottie: A React Native player. It uses Skia's Skottie module to play Lottie. Install react-native-skia first. The author says it is faster on a low-end Android phone, so measure that yourself. It has had few updates since January 2025. It is a player, not After Effects. The license is MIT.
maximeraafat/BlenderNeRF: A Blender add-on. One click exports images and cameras for a synthetic NeRF or Gaussian-splatting dataset. It needs Blender 4.0 or newer. It has had few updates since December 2024. It is a dataset tool, not a trainer. The license is MIT.
markaren/threepp: A C++20 3D library. The API follows three.js, with OpenGL and Vulkan backends and Python bindings. The catalog lists it under Gaussian splatting, but it is a general scene library, not a splatting trainer. The license is MIT.
AlayaLab/Evoke: An interactive world model. It uses three steps and does not use CFG. The author says one H200 produces about 1.5 seconds of video in 2.11 seconds, and the WBench figure is theirs, so measure it yourself. It has had few updates since September 2026. It is the world model itself. The license is Apache-2.0.
Nanako0129/sepia: An agent skill for rewriting. Fiction gets its narrative structure repaired first, and documents follow rules for their setting. The four operations are write, review, a small edit, and a full rewrite. Any agent that can read SKILL.md can use it. It is a skill, not a new model. The license is MIT.
yetone/cumora: Team chat. Agents and people share groups, direct messages, and a board. The cloud path uses the OpenAI interface, or you run Claude Code, Codex, and similar tools on your own machine. The server does not see your provider keys. It is a chat shell, not a new model. The license is MIT.
wzzheng/StreamVGGT: A streaming 4D geometry model. A new image uses cached memory, so the whole clip is not recomputed. It was accepted to ICLR 2026. Weights are on Hugging Face. It is different from VGGT already in the catalog. The license is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: no commercial use, and adaptations stay under the same license. It has had few updates since October 2025.
Gamote/lottie-react: A React player. It wraps lottie-web and plays a JSON file. It needs React 18.2 or newer. It is different from lottie-react-native in the catalog: this one is for the web. You supply the animation. It is a player, not After Effects. The license is MIT.
VAST-AI-Research/MIDI-3D: A research model. One image generates several 3D objects and their positions at the same time. It was presented at CVPR 2025. Weights are on Hugging Face as VAST-AI/MIDI-3D. It is different from TripoSplat already in the catalog. It has had few updates since June 2025. The license is Apache-2.0.
VAST-AI-Research/TriplaneGaussian: A research model. One image becomes 3D Gaussians in a few seconds. Weights are on Hugging Face as VAST-AI/TriplaneGaussian. The author says about one second, so measure it yourself. It has had few updates since March 2024. It is a reconstruction model, not a viewer. The license is Apache-2.0.
PatilShreyas/MaterialDialog-Android: An Android dialog library. It can play a Lottie animation, and you still export that animation from After Effects. It has had few updates since January 2022. The catalog lists it under motion graphics, but it is a UI library, not an editor. The license is Apache-2.0.
peylnog/ContinuousSR: Research code for image super-resolution. It rebuilds a continuous high-resolution image from a low-resolution one with 2D Gaussians. It was accepted to ICLR 2026. Only test code and weights are released, and the training code is not. The catalog lists it under Gaussian splatting, but it is not 3D splatting. The repository includes no open-source license file.
Junchao-cs/SolarWM: A framework for interactive world models, with long-video generation, training, and real-time deployment. Data and weights are on Hugging Face, and some of the data requires an application. It is a world-model framework, not a chatbot. The license is Apache-2.0. Measure the result yourself.
NucleoidAI/Nucleoid: A logic language. It writes objects and relationships in few tokens, and execution is declarative. A world model can use it to store structure. There is a terminal workspace, installed with cargo install nucleoid. It is a language, not a video world model. The license is Apache-2.0.
juliobsz/skills: An agent skill. One brief becomes a website. It needs Node.js 22.20 or newer. Claude Code, Codex, and other agents that read SKILL.md can use it. It is a skill, not a new model. The license is MIT.
Leonxlnx/unlazy: An agent skill. It makes an agent write an acceptance list first, check the work after, and report only then. The core is SKILL.md. It needs Node.js 16 or newer. It is a skill, not a new model. The license is MIT.
Derpyu520/qq-bridge: A local bridge. It forwards QQ messages to DeepSeek Harness through the public OneBot v11 protocol. It is not an official Tencent, QQ, SnowLuma, or DeepSeek product. You run both services yourself, on Windows, with Node.js 22.13 or newer. The license is PolyForm Noncommercial, so commercial use is not allowed.
VAST-AI-Research/EdenLive: A real-time generative renderer. A reference video goes in and an appearance video comes out, while the world state stays in your program. Weights are on Hugging Face as VAST-AI/EdenLive. The author says an RTX 5090 can reach 24 fps or higher, so measure it yourself. It is a render model, not a game engine. The license is Apache-2.0.
ziangcao0312/PhysX-Anything: A research model. One image becomes a physical 3D asset you can drop into a simulation. It was accepted to CVPR 2026. The dataset is on Hugging Face. It has had few updates since April 2026. The license is S-Lab License 1.0, and use is limited to non-commercial purposes.
DengKaiCQ/VGGT-Long: It uses the existing VGGT model on kilometer-scale RGB sequences, in chunks, with alignment and loop closure. It does not retrain the model and does not need camera calibration. It is different from VGGT and StreamVGGT already in the catalog. It has had few updates since March 2026. The license is the VGGT License.
OpenDCAI/OpenWorldLib: A shared codebase for world models. Training and inference live in one place. The catalog lists it under Gaussian splatting, but it is not a splatting trainer and it is not one new model. The license is Apache-2.0.
caiyuanhao1998/Open-DiffusionGS: A research model. It bakes Gaussian splatting into a diffusion denoiser, so one image becomes 3D in a single stage. It was presented at ICCV 2025. The data is on Hugging Face. It is a generator, not a viewer. The license is MIT.
Dakkshin/after-effects-mcp: An MCP server. It uses ExtendScript to control After Effects while you have it open, and it can add compositions, text, and shapes. You need your own copy of After Effects. It has had few updates since April 2026. It is a remote control, not After Effects itself. The license is MIT.
facebookresearch/nwm: A navigation world model. Conditional diffusion predicts the view after a move. It was a CVPR 2025 oral. Weights are on Hugging Face as facebook/nwm. It has had few updates since November 2025. The license is CC BY-NC 4.0, so commercial use is not allowed. It is the world model itself.
leggedrobotics/robotic_world_model: An Isaac Lab extension. It learns robot policies with a neural dynamics model. You can train it together with the simulator, or offline with the learned model. It needs Isaac Sim. It is a robotic world model, not a video model. The license is Apache-2.0.
Belluxx/Aleph: A local tool. Draw an area on the map and it downloads buildings, terrain, a satellite image, Street View photos, and a textured 3D mesh, for you or for an LLM. It needs Python 3.11 or newer and no API key. The code is MIT. OSM data is ODbL. Terrain uses AWS open tiles. The author says Street View, satellite imagery, and the 3D meshes belong to Google, downloading them breaks Google's terms, and the tool uses undocumented interfaces, so it can break. It is a downloader listed under Image, not an image model.
NiazMorshed2007/reanimate: A Claude Code skill for copying an animation. Give it a web page, a recording, an mp4, a gif, or a Lottie file. It films the motion, then rebuilds it with the CSS, Framer Motion, GSAP, or three.js you already use, and compares the copy. It needs Bun 1.1 or newer, on macOS or Linux, and no API key. The license is MIT. Other people's assets still belong to their owners. It is a skill, not a new motion model.
Appllama/appllama-skills: Two agent skills for mobile screens. The research skill needs the Appllama MCP and your own Pro account. The design skill writes Expo and React Native screens and works without the MCP. Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex can install them. The code is MIT. The name and logo are trademarks, and the license does not include them. It is not a new model.
KKKKhazix/human-writing: A Chinese writing skill. It asks the model to sound like one specific person speaking. Real topics have to be checked against the facts, and fiction still needs action and change. The draft then cuts repetition, report-voice, and reversal sentences. Any agent that reads SKILL.md can install it, and a short version can be pasted into a chat window. The license is MIT. It is not a new language model. It has had few updates since August 2026.
gsgen3d/gsgen: CVPR 2024 text-to-3D Gaussians. It starts from the existing Point-E or Shap-E model and then trains, and it can export ply and splat. The mesh export is shape only for now. The author says the viewer can pass 40 frames per second on an M1 Pro, so measure it yourself. The license is MIT. It has had few updates since January 2024. It is different from GaussianDreamer.
hustvl/GaussianDreamer: CVPR 2024. One sentence becomes 3D Gaussians. It uses the existing Shap-E model as the 3D start, then a 2D diffusion model fills in geometry and appearance, and it can also make a human avatar. The author says one GPU takes about 15 minutes, so measure it yourself. There is a Hugging Face demo. The license is Apache-2.0. It has had few updates since January 2025. It is different from GSGEN.
EnVision-Research/LucidDreamer: A CVPR 2024 highlight. Interval score matching distills a high-quality 3D asset from text, on top of 3D Gaussians and an existing 2D diffusion model. The author says an A100 takes about 35 minutes, so measure it yourself. The license is MIT. It has had few updates since May 2024. This is text-to-3D, and it is different from the scene version at luciddreamer-cvlab.
NVlabs/PartPacker: One image generates a 3D object split into parts. The weights are on Hugging Face at nvidia/PartPacker, and inference is about 10 GB. The author tested it on a 3090 and a 4090. The NVIDIA Source Code License allows non-commercial use only, while NVIDIA itself may use it commercially. It has had few updates since June 2025. It is different from TRELLIS.
IamCreateAI/NeoVerse: A CVPR 2026 highlight, and the best paper of the VideoWorldModel workshop. It reconstructs a monocular clip, then renders a video along a new camera path. The weights are on Hugging Face at Yuppie1204/NeoVerse, and it uses the existing Wan 2.1. The author says one A800 can finish in under 30 seconds, so measure it yourself. The license is Apache-2.0.
heqiangdiao-wq/AI-Cross-Border-Ecommerce: A cross-border ecommerce skill pack with seven workflows: market, strategy, title, main image, short video, ads, and reviews. You fill in a template and hand it to any LLM, with no API key. Calculation scripts handle price bands and net margin, and the model only interprets them. The whole folder can be installed as SKILL.md. The license is MIT, and it is still beta. It is not a store program and not a new model.
hardbeat920/monocode: A desktop interface for coding agents. Tools you already installed and signed into, such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, can run side by side in tabs. It does not sell tokens. The license is MIT. It is still early. The native preview is experimental and writes into the same database, so back up before you try it. It is not a new model.
freestylefly/WeChatBridge: A share extension for macOS and Windows. WeChat 4.1.13 or newer already exports a chat ZIP, and this app receives it, pastes it into the Codex or Claude you already have, or saves Obsidian Markdown. It does not read the WeChat database and does not inject into WeChat. It is not official Tencent. The license is MIT. You need your own WeChat and the target app.
mystorm16/FastVGGT: ICLR 2026. It speeds up long-sequence reconstruction with the existing VGGT model and does not retrain it. The author says it can be about 4 times faster, so measure it yourself. It needs the VGGT weights on Hugging Face. The license is the VGGT License. It is different from VGGT, StreamVGGT, and VGGT-Long already in the catalog. It has had few updates since January 2026. It is not a new geometry model.
Lewis-Stuart-11/3DGS-to-PC: It turns a 3D Gaussian ply or splat into a dense point cloud, and with Open3D it can also make a mesh. Colours need the camera transforms, or they will not look like the original scene. If the CUDA extension will not install, a pure Python renderer is available. The license is Apache-2.0. It is from ICCVW 2025. It has had few updates since November 2025. It is a converter, not a trainer.
NVlabs/LongSplat: ICCV 2025. A casual long video with no camera poses is reconstructed as 3D Gaussians. Poses come from the existing MASt3R model. The result can be converted for ordinary 3DGS viewers. The NVIDIA License allows only non-commercial research or evaluation, while NVIDIA may use it commercially. It has had few updates since January 2026.
UMass-Embodied-AGI/3D-VLA: An embodied world model from ICML 2024. It is built on the existing 3D-LLM, predicts a goal image and a point cloud, then outputs an action. The weights are on Hugging Face at anyezhy. The repository has no license file. It has had few updates since October 2024. It is not a video world model.
NoizAI/HelixWorld: A real-time audio-visual world model. Give it an image and a prompt, then walk or turn, and the picture and the spatial sound change together. The preview weights are on Hugging Face at NoizAI/HelixWorld-preview. The code is Apache-2.0, and the weight license is separate. The text encoder is the existing Gemma 3. The author says an H800 can do 24 frames per second, so measure it yourself. It needs about 70 GB of VRAM.
HarnessRouter/harnessrouter: A self-hosted interface. One API runs harnesses you already have, such as Codex and Claude Code. It needs Docker, about 4 GB of disk, and your own provider key. There is no bundled model. The license is Apache-2.0. Change the default login before you expose it. It is not a new model.
vercel-labs/fx: An experimental Unix-style coding agent. It is one Zig binary for macOS and Linux, with no runtime to install. The model is yours: Vercel, ChatGPT, Grok, or a compatible endpoint. It can read skills, but it is the agent. By default it edits files and runs tests without asking. The license is Apache-2.0. It is not a new model.
kirodotdev/KiroCrew: A development workspace on your own machine, local or remote. Tasks can continue across sessions, and they can run unattended. The default agent is kiro-cli, which you install and sign in to separately. It runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows. It sends one anonymous usage heartbeat a day, and you can turn that off. The license is Apache-2.0. It is not a new model.
ginwind/VLA-JEPA: ECCV 2026. A latent world model that strengthens a vision-language-action model. It is based on the existing starVLA project and needs Qwen3-VL-2B and V-JEPA2. The weights are on Hugging Face at ginwind/VLA-JEPA. The code is Apache-2.0, and third-party portions keep their own licenses. It has had few updates since September 2026. It is not a video world model.
NVIDIA/GR00T-Dreams: It uses the existing Cosmos world model. One image and an instruction become a robot video, then actions are extracted to fine-tune GR00T N1. This repository is that pipeline, not a new video model. The license is Apache-2.0. It has had few updates since October 2025.
lennney/stop-that-shit: A skill and a guard for coding agents. It stops unrequested checksums, scope creep, file edits during a read-only review, and repeats of checks that are already done. Codex, Claude Code, and similar tools can use it. The license is MIT. It is a skill, not a new model.
ctoldigital/axuse: A local MCP. It drives a browser and a computer from the accessibility tree, not a screenshot loop. It needs Node.js 22 or newer and Chromium. MCP hosts such as Codex and Claude Code can use it. Windows desktop control has been tested. macOS needs an extra permission. The license is PolyForm Noncommercial, so commercial use is not allowed. It is not a new model.
typesafe-ai/skills: One agent skill for designing a TypeSafe System One integration: states, questions, and requests. You need your own TypeSafe account and API. Claude Code can install it as a plugin, and other agents use skills.sh. It is different from the three other repositories in this catalog that are also named skills. The license is MIT. It is not the model itself.
oil-oil/oil-motion: A skill for interactive web animation. You say what it should express and which input it follows. The agent uses a video model you already have to make the frames, then connects them to scroll, the mouse, or a drag. The browser only plays the finished frames. It is listed under Video. It is not After Effects and not a new video model. The license is MIT.
ArcReel/ArcReel: A self-hosted short-video workspace. A novel or a script becomes characters, a storyboard, and a video, and it can export a mainland-China Jianying draft. CapCut compatibility is not verified. The video comes from model APIs you connect yourself. It needs Docker. The license is AGPL-3.0. It is not a new video model.
InternRobotics/Aether: ICCV 2025, and an outstanding paper of that workshop. One world model does 4D reconstruction, predicts the next clip from an action, and plans from a goal image. The weights are on Hugging Face at AetherWorldModel/AetherV1. The code is MIT. It has had few updates since October 2025. The author says it can generalize to real scenes without extra training, so measure it yourself.
N1nEmAn/sapper-v2: A multi-agent attack-and-defense program. A commander splits work across a group, using Claude Code you already installed. The author says an unattended run finished a Tencent intelligent attack-defense qualifier. Use it only on systems you own or have written permission to test. MIT. It is an agent, not a new language model.
speridlabs/idol-sdk: One object photo becomes 3D Gaussians and a standard ply. Python 3.10 or newer and PyTorch 2.5 or newer. Weights are on Hugging Face at speridlabs/idol. The code is Apache-2.0. DINOv3 and FLUX.2-dev need separate access, and their licenses stay theirs. The author says peak use is about 7.2 GB of VRAM. This inference kit is a different project from TripoSplat.
huaxialucaicaizi/ai-startup-skills: An agent skill pack with seven steps plus a router: validation, a business plan, policy, a pitch, growth, pricing, and registration. It is for one-person companies building AI products in China, on Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor. Policy and tax notes are information, not professional advice. MIT. It is not a new model.
AminBlg/SimpleEnglish: A writing skill that asks a model you already have to write technical instructions in short sentences and the active voice, in the style of Simplified Technical English. It installs on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other agents that read skills. MIT. Unofficial, not affiliated with ASD, and the standard text is not in the repo. It is not a new model.
zhuyansen/awesome-claude-video-skills: A directory of other people's video skills for Claude Code, Codex, and similar coding agents. The list text is CC0. Each listed project keeps its own license. The author says every entry has a security grade, and the page is updated. This is a catalog, not a video model.
cbrock84/headcount: An agent skill pack: 16 departments and 172 skills, and you can install only the departments you need. It runs in Claude Code, ChatGPT, and Codex. It cites outside standards and regulations, but the text is written once and does not track a regulator's latest publication. MIT. It is not a new model.
hanzohanzhe/Grandet: A skill, plus an anonymous MCP, that compares published prices for model APIs across official providers, inference hosts, and resellers, then connects a key you already have. Install needs Node.js 20 or newer, or you can copy the skill folder. The skill is Apache-2.0. The catalogue program is AGPL-3.0-only. The price data is under neither license. It is not a new model.
Jakubantalik/thinking-orbs: Loading animations for AI interfaces: nine states and two sizes, drawn on a plain canvas. It ships as an npm package for React. It follows light and dark theme, and it holds one frame when the user prefers less motion. MIT. The last push was in August 2026. It is a UI component, not an agent and not a model.
zvec-ai/zvec-grep: Local search built on the existing zvec engine: text search, BM25, and vector search in one interface. Use it in the terminal or over MCP from an agent. Node.js 22 or newer. The index and local models stay on your machine. Remote embeddings are sent only if you allow it. Apache-2.0. It is a search tool, not a new language model.
Player-YN/BrowserKitten: A Chrome side-panel web agent. It works on a tab where you are already logged in, and it needs your own OpenAI-compatible key. It is not in the Chrome Web Store. Load it in developer mode. Chrome 135 or newer. MIT. The README calls it PawWork, and it is a different project from browser-use. The last push was in September 2026. It is a browser agent, not a new model.
athemeroy/awesome-claude-5-5-videos: A directory of other people's videos and animations made with Claude 5.5, with source posts and production notes. The author says that as of 11 October 2026 there were 424 distinct sources, and nine-frame previews do not show the full film. Fable entries are only what creators reported. The list is CC-BY-4.0. It is a different project from awesome-claude-video-skills, and it is not a video model.
yihui-dev/awesome-opus5-5-videos: A directory of other people's videos, drawn as web animation with Claude Opus 5.5, plus links to the original posts. The author says there are 703 prompts, and 418 have a remake on Skillry. The videos and prompts belong to their creators. The list code is MIT. It is a different project from awesome-claude-5-5-videos, and it is not a video model. The last push was on 13 October 2026.
alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered: An index of open-source clients and tools other people already published, with a search page, a skill, and an MCP server. The author says it now lists more than seventeen thousand projects. The program is MIT. The index data is CC0. Each listed project keeps its own license. This is an index, not a new model.
chengyi-ai/native-subtitle-quote-image: An agent skill that turns video frames into a tall social image. Native mode only crops subtitles already burned into the picture. Script mode draws lines you have already checked, and the two modes are not mixed. A local file or a YouTube link both work, and the Python scripts can run on their own. Codex and Claude Code. MIT. It is not a new model.
openqodex/openqodex: A local code review that uses another agent you already signed into, before you push. Claude Code and Codex can be the reviewer. Cursor and Cline can only start the review. Node.js 22 or newer, on macOS or Linux. It has no account or key of its own. Apache-2.0. It is not a new model.
LearnPrompt/awesome-seedance: A Seedance case directory. The author says it has more than 840 source posts, 27 templates, and 79 skills, synced daily from goodcase.ai. You still generate the video yourself with the existing Seedance model on Jimeng or Dreamina. The list is MIT. It is a directory, not a new video model.
Alisa0808/vox-director: An agent skill that turns one topic into a paper-collage explainer. You approve the beats and the look first. Pictures, motion, narration, and music come from existing models through your own Atlas Cloud key, and ffmpeg assembles the film. It needs Python 3, Pillow, and ffmpeg. MIT. It is not a new video model.
guanmo-ai/awesome-ai-motion: A directory of motion design and creative videos. The author says the gallery has 1,728 works, with original posts and prompts. The works stay with those posts. The list program is MIT. It is a different project from awesome-opus5-5-videos. It is a directory, not a video model. The last push was on 27 October 2026.
mikehasa/golive-skill: An agent skill that puts a product your agent built online: hosting, a database, a domain, email, and payments, all on accounts you already have. It writes only after you approve. Node.js 20 or newer. Codex and Claude Code have been tried. Early alpha. No GoLive account and no telemetry. Keys sit in a plaintext file outside the repo. MIT. It is not a new model.
franzenzenhofer/big-arrow-on-the-screen: A macOS skill and command-line tool. Claude Code and Codex can draw big arrows, boxes, and text on the screen. Clicks pass through, and the marks go away on their own. Finding an element needs Accessibility permission. MIT. It only points. It does not press for you. It is not a new model.
dagoSte/squadra: A local coordinator used so Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor windows can share one project's tasks, checks, and reviews on your machine. It ships a skill, a CLI, and a local dashboard. Needs Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or POSIX, and uses only the standard library. MIT. This is not a new model.
jtydhr88/screenwriting-skills: A pack of 26 agent skills for screenwriting, television writing, and dramaturgy, for Claude Code and Codex. The skill text is written in Chinese and lives in the repo; ask in another language and the agent answers in that language. Install once and both agents can use it. MIT. These are writing skills, not a new model.
Harvil1/codeAgent: A terminal coding agent you talk to in natural language so it reads code, edits files, and runs commands on your machine. You bring your own OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-protocol model; DeepSeek is the default. It includes approvals, memory, and skills. Windows first, Python 3.11 or newer. MIT. This is not a new model.
yeyuxin777/baoyan-agent-benchmark: An open benchmark for agent setups that advise on Baoyan admissions and application planning. It has 70 Chinese tasks, 23 cases, and 83 answer stages. The public data needs no approval, but scoring materials stay hidden from the agent under test. You run it on your own existing agent. MIT. This is a test set, not a new model.
Jakeschincariol/arena-skill: A Claude Code skill that runs up to 100 sub-agents on the same task in a knockout bracket, each with a different strategy, and leaves you one answer to accept or ignore. Sub-agents only write inside .arena/ and do not change your files. Needs Claude Code and Python 3.8 or newer. MIT. This is not a new model.
N4darae/shrt: An API regression tool that records call chains such as login, create, and read-back. You approve one passing run as the baseline, then replay it on your machine, and a change tells you which step moved. shrt init installs a Claude Code skill, and the commands also run by hand. Needs Go 1.26 and buf. It speaks Connect today, not plain gRPC. MIT. This is not a new model.
zeronsh/zeron: A local control plane for coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Devin. The desktop app runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux with no account. NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns the current session into a captain, splitting tasks, assigning sub-agents, and passing messages inside the host. Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-design-world: A local video and design plugin for DeepSeek Harness. It edits, lays out templates, previews, and exports real files on your machine. It needs Node.js 22 and FFmpeg 7. caru-ini/stack-diagram: An agent skill that turns one sentence about your stack into an architecture diagram with official logos. achimala/dream-loop: An agent skill for a game, app, or scene with strong visuals. The agent needs vision and image generation; custom 3D needs Blender installed by you. The author only tested GPT-6 Astra in Codex. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
QwenAudio/qwen-audio-agent: A realtime voice runtime so the conversation keeps going while an agent is working. It needs Node.js 22.22.2 or newer. Voice and the backend use your own API key. The default voice model is Qwen Audio 3.1, and other existing voice models can be connected. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
CookSleep/gpt_image_playground: A web tool for generating and editing images in the browser. It calls OpenAI gpt-image-2.5 or a compatible endpoint, fal.ai, and HTTP providers you import. The key is yours, and history and settings stay on your machine. MIT. This is an interface and does not give you a new image model.
blendi-remade/agentcraft: A Minecraft interface where Claude or Codex agents edit your repo inside the game. It needs Minecraft Java, Java 25, Node 22, and git. Agents use your Claude API access or a Codex login you already have. Nothing is pushed until you press Merge. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
coldteadotai/pr-lens: A tool and skill that draws a pull request as architecture and data-flow diagrams and posts them on the pull request. The GitHub App does not need your model key. The skill uses the coding agent you already have. The CLI and Action can use your own model instead. Building it yourself needs Node 20.11 or newer. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
dualface/ste-zh: An agent skill that makes an agent report in simplified technical Chinese: conclusion first, with evidence, and a fixed status. It borrows the ASD-STE100 rules and only changes how the agent talks to you, not code, comments, or commits. It does nothing until you turn it on. The Traditional Chinese edition is ste-zht. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-Desktop: A DeepSeek Harness desktop workbench for chat, files, tools, and plugins in one window. The installer bundles Node and dsh, so a normal install does not need them separately. Models are called through the provider you connect. Windows has v6.0.0; the Linux and macOS packages are older. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
simonlin1212/Vibe-Research: A research workbench for China A-shares, US stocks, and Hong Kong stocks: watchlists, holdings, daily review, backtests, and research notes. The author lists 168 data endpoints, and the records stay on your machine. AI uses your own Claude Code, Codex, or a compatible API, and you can browse without connecting one. Needs Node.js 22.18 and Python 3.11. MIT. It does not place orders and does not give you a new model.
islandmed/SculptForge: An open-source sculpting app for Linux, macOS, and Windows that also handles Gaussian splats. The built-in AI defaults to GPT-OSS 20B on Pollinations and uses local Ollama offline. Image-to-3D can use your own ComfyUI or a local model. GPL-3.0. This does not give you a new model.
Tiger3807861189/J-Space-Cognition-Suite: An agent skill suite that organizes evidence and checks for a long task at inference time. It needs Python 3.10 or newer and has no pip dependencies. The host you already use supplies the model and tools, and installing the files does not start an agent. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
dream-num/univer-workspace: An open-source Office workspace for sheets, documents, slides, and boards in one runtime. An agent edits in an isolated worktree, and you review the change before it is merged. It needs Node.js 24 or newer, and the model key is yours. Run it locally or on your own server. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
Leonxlnx/cinetic: An agent skill that has a coding agent make a short film with Remotion or HyperFrames. It works in Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. You need Node 22, ffmpeg 6, Python 3.11, and Chromium. The film renders on your machine. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
Aryanutkarsh/SeeCode: An agent skill that turns a short spec into an animated diagram you can explore. One HTML file can be hovered and clicked in the browser, then exported as SVG, PNG, GIF, or MP4. Chart numbers come from CSV or JSON and do not pass through the model. It works in Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
Pinvou/pinvou-agent: A desktop agent for files, a knowledge base, and workflows on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It can use local vLLM or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and the key is yours. wuyoscar/GPT-Image2-Skill: Two agent skills and a command-line tool that ask GPT Image 2 or 2.5 to generate and edit images from Claude Code or Codex, plus a prompt gallery. It needs Python 3.11 and your own OpenAI key. MIT. This does not give you a new image model.
MiniMax-AI/mcode-stack: A skill pack that installs the workflows the MiniMax Code team uses into MiniMax Code, Claude Code, or Codex. Each piece is a SKILL.md, not a prompt collection, and it installs on your machine. The model is still the agent you already signed in to. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
feder-cr/invisible_playwright_mcp: An MCP server that lets Claude Code or Codex open Firefox on your machine, click through pages, and read them. Install it with uv. The project is built to make sites less likely to treat the browser as a bot. MIT. This is only a browser tool, not a new model.
redhat-et/ripwire: A local command-line tool and optional MCP server that helps a coding agent find what to read before it opens the whole repo. It runs offline and has no runtime dependencies. shijue-aid/aid-studio: A self-hosted platform for AI motion comics, short dramas, and comics: scripts, storyboards, images, video, and voiceover. Text, image, video, and speech all use model keys you provide. Deploy it with Docker or systemd. MIT. This does not give you a new video model.
zhanghao123vip/ai-manju-skills: Twenty-one genre skills that turn one idea into a plan, asset-image prompts, episode scripts, storyboards, and video prompts. benjitaylor/skills: The Stageshow agent skill asks your coding agent to build fake product UI in React: stills, feature cards, cursor demos, and bento grids. It can film the result so the agent can check its work. Install it with npx skills. The skill file is MIT. This is not a new model.
miuuyy/Octopus-SI-OS: A research-preview agent system that runs agents such as Codex on macOS 14 or newer. They can read and write files and use the browser and desktop. 0xsline/OpenChatCut: A local video editor for cutting on a multitrack timeline. Codex, Claude Code, or the built-in agent can edit, and the changes stay in the project. Desktop installers are available; building it needs Node.js 24. Projects and media stay on your machine by default. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a new video model.
maxrave-dev/kotlin-footguns: Ten agent skills plus a scanner that warn about traps in Kotlin, Compose Multiplatform, and the desktop JVM. The author says they were mined from his production music app, not copied from docs. Install with npx skills for agents such as Claude Code. GPL-3.0. This does not give you a new model.
chipfighter/framekeeper: An agent plugin that manages images in a chat: earlier images are not uploaded again every turn, and the model pulls one back when it needs it. It works with Codex, Claude Code, WorkBuddy, and Gemini CLI. The images still go to the model you already use. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
HanyuanWang/LiveStream-Agent-Studio: A local Windows workspace for Douyin livestream commerce: find hosts, break down a stream, review it, and plan short videos. It needs your own Alibaba Cloud Model Studio key. v0.2.0 beta, and the launcher is not commercially signed. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
ZeroDayEvil/ai-security-tool: A cross-platform terminal and supply-chain scanner for checking known vulnerabilities and an SBOM on your machine. It can also open SSH, SFTP, RDP, and VNC sessions. The AI needs your own DeepSeek or OpenAI key. MIT. This is not an attack guide and does not give you a new model.
whaleyxbt/claude-motion: A motion-design skill that teaches your coding agent to make a film in Remotion, review its own frames, and synthesize sound with the Python standard library. Claude Code and Cursor include the skills. It needs Node 20, Python 3, and ffmpeg. MIT. This does not give you a new video model.
QoderAI/better-harness: A plugin that looks at the work loop, evidence, and next steps inside the coding agent you already use. It supports hosts such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. It does not include a model, and missing evidence stays explicit. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
eliasstravik/shepherdr: A control panel for herdr-core so you can watch coding agents across machines from a phone, tablet, or computer. Each task runs in its own git worktree and is reviewed before it merges. It needs herdr-core 0.1.14, Bun, and macOS or Linux. Tailscale keeps it on your private network. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
richiemcilroy/Tov: Tov is a TypeScript-shaped language that compiles to a small native program. Version 0.1.0 runs on macOS arm64 and Linux, and Windows is not supported yet. Building it yourself needs Rust 1.95 and a C compiler, and TypeScript parity is still incomplete. MIT. This is a compiler. It does not give you a new model.
gnipbao/story-to-handdrawn-video: An agent skill that turns a Chinese story or ordered images into a 3:4 silent hand-drawn MP4 inside Codex, Claude Code, or a similar agent. NVIDIA-NeMo/labs-OO-Agents: A Python framework for writing an AI agent as a class. Fields hold state, and a method whose body is an ellipsis is handed to the model. The model needs your own API key. kgoedecke/doop: A multiplayer design canvas where you and an AI agent edit frames together in the browser. It has a built-in MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and similar clients. sahenjp/RustXNG: A local metasearch engine that lets an AI agent search the web on your machine. It is a Rust rewrite of SearXNG and can optionally fetch page text. This does not give you a new model.
tourmind-com/Tourmind-Booking-Skills: Two agent skills that search hotels and flights inside the agent you already use, then book and pay through TourMind. Search can start without a token. feimacode/open-design-agent-kit: A design skill kit that makes pitch decks, web pages, and prototypes inside the coding agent you already use. It supports Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. AMAP-ML/LongHorizon-Harness: An execution loop that runs long tasks on Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or DeepSeek Harness. Each step starts with a fresh context, and only a checked result counts as progress. It needs Python 3.10 and the agent you already have. Version 0.1.8 still has Windows limits. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
MemTensor/memmy-agent: A local memory hub that shares one memory across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and similar agents. The desktop app is the main way to use it. iAmCorey/Wake: A desktop app that gathers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other agent sessions on one machine, then resumes them in a terminal. RinDig/icm-architect: An agent skill that turns a task into a folder layout inside Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor. Each folder is a step or a piece of state a person can open. Optional Python 3 standard-library scripts can check the result. It does not include an orchestrator. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
op7418/guizang-social-card-skill: An agent skill that makes Xiaohongshu carousels and WeChat cover pairs inside Claude Code or Codex. It writes one HTML file and renders PNGs with Playwright. It needs Node. It uses the model your agent already has, and it looks up a photo library only when you did not supply images. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a new model.
Sahir619/fable-method: A skill pack that runs a think, act, and prove workflow on the model you already have, with an eval beside it. Install it as Claude Code plugin 1.4.0. It does not include Fable. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
croffasia/itsaplan: A self-hosted project board where people and AI agents follow issues on the same board. It exposes REST, webhooks, and MCP. Self-hosting needs Bun or Docker. It does not include a model. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a new model.
boyang-hu/website-rebuild-skill: An agent skill that takes a read-only mirror of a website inside the coding agent you already use, rebuilds it into editable files, and checks the result with a visual diff. The files stay on your machine. It needs Node 22. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
l0ng-ai/tty7: A terminal workbench that keeps shells alive on macOS, Windows, or Linux after you close the window. An agent you already have can drive another one, including on a remote machine. It is pure Rust. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
ASLP-lab/WenetSpeech-Yue: A large Cantonese corpus and model set for recognition and synthesis on your machine. It is about 21,800 hours and includes CosyVoice2-Yue plus the ZoengJyutGaai fine-tune. QwenAudio/SenseVoice: A speech-understanding model that transcribes audio on your machine and marks language and emotion. SenseVoiceSmall supports Cantonese, Mandarin, English, Japanese, and Korean. MIT. This recognizes speech. It does not synthesize a voice.
QwenAudio/CosyVoice: Multilingual speech generation that does zero-shot cloning from a reference clip. It covers many Chinese dialects, including Cantonese, and it can cross languages. You download the weights yourself. Apache-2.0. This does not give you one fixed Hong Kong speaker.
RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS: Few-shot voice cloning that uses a reference clip of your own on your machine. About five seconds can do zero-shot, and about one minute can fine-tune. Cantonese is in the language list. A GPU makes it practical. MIT. This does not give you a fixed speaker.
OpenBMB/VoxCPM: A local TTS that clones a voice from a short reference clip, or designs a new voice from a text description. VoxCPM2 is about 2B parameters, outputs 48 kHz, and its Chinese dialects include Cantonese. You run the model yourself. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a hosted service.
indiejoseph/JyutVoice: A Cantonese TTS that synthesizes Cantonese, Mandarin, or English from a reference clip. It transfers from a CosyVoice2 decoder. It needs Python 3.11 and a separate weight download. The project is still small. MIT. This does not give you a cloud service.
openai/whisper: General speech-to-text that turns a recording into text on your machine. It supports many languages, and Cantonese is not a dedicated target. You download the weights yourself. MIT. This recognizes speech. It does not give you a new voice.
coqui-ai/TTS: A speech-synthesis toolkit for training and running TTS in research or a product. It includes several models and voices, and you choose the weights. MPL-2.0. It is not a Cantonese specialist, and it does not automatically give you a Hong Kong accent.
2noise/ChatTTS: Dialogue speech synthesis that generates everyday conversation on your machine. The code is AGPL-3.0. The released model weights are CC-BY-NC, so they are not for commercial use. It is not a Cantonese model. This does not clone a named person.
RVC-Project/Retrieval-based-Voice-Conver: A voice converter that trains a timbre on your machine from about ten minutes of clean speech, then converts singing or speech. The base model comes from VCTK. It has a web UI. MIT. It is not a Cantonese synthesizer, and it does not turn text into speech.
myshell-ai/OpenVoice: Instant timbre cloning that takes a voice color from a short reference clip and adds style control. V2 includes Chinese natively, and it is not built for Cantonese. MIT, including commercial use. You run it yourself. This does not ship a finished Hong Kong accent.
SYSTRAN/faster-whisper: A faster Whisper implementation that transcribes speech on your machine with CTranslate2. It is quicker than the original, and Cantonese is still not a dedicated target. MIT. This does not synthesize a voice.
facebookresearch/audiocraft: A music and sound generation library that runs MusicGen and AudioGen from text or a melody. The code is MIT. The weights are CC-BY-NC, so they are not for commercial use. It is not voice cloning, and it does not give you Cantonese TTS.
modelscope/FunASR: A speech-recognition toolkit that chains VAD, ASR, punctuation, and speaker diarization on your machine, including streaming. MIT. Cantonese needs a separate model such as SenseVoice. This toolkit does not automatically give you a Cantonese voice.
neonbjb/tortoise-tts: A multi-voice TTS that favors quality and generates speech slowly on your machine. Apache-2.0. It is not mainly Cantonese, and it is not real time. You run the weights yourself. This does not give you a Hong Kong accent.
SWivid/F5-TTS: A flow-matching TTS that does zero-shot synthesis from a reference clip. The code is MIT. The pretrained weights are CC-BY-NC, so they are not for commercial use. It is mainly Chinese and English, not a Cantonese specialist. This does not give you commercial weights.
multimodal-art-projection/YuE: A music model that plans a song from lyrics and style. YuE2 can also do a zero-shot cover and edit a track. You run it yourself. Apache-2.0. This is music. It does not give you Cantonese speech synthesis.
hexgrad/kokoro: A small TTS of about 82M parameters for low-cost speech on your machine. Apache-2.0. It is not a Cantonese model, and you download the weights yourself. This does not clone a Hong Kong speaker.
OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl: A local neural TTS that reads text quickly on a CPU. The current line is GPL-3.0. Voices are downloaded separately, and Cantonese is not a default voice. This does not clone a person.
ace-step/ACE-Step: A music foundation model that generates music from a text condition. Apache-2.0. You run the weights yourself. This is for composition. It does not tell a story in Cantonese.
Superior-Trade/trading-terminal: A self-hosted Hyperliquid terminal that turns a drawing on your chart into a Freqtrade strategy. This does not give you a new model.
modelflare-ai/AnyModelBot: A local-first desktop agent that keeps a bot running on Windows, macOS, or Linux. leemysw/yovoice: A local voice and music studio for speech, cloning, and songs on your machine. macOS 14 needs Apple silicon. Windows and Linux are x64. Models download separately, and some weights are not for commercial use. v0.5.0. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model without a download.
C4rohan/Lampline: A phone-agent studio for writing and testing phone agents on your machine. Local tests can run without an API key. inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts: A multilingual TTS that clones or designs a voice on your machine, and Cantonese is one of the languages. It has a 0.5B model and a smaller MoE. agentverse-os/AgentVerse-OS: A personal cloud desktop that runs coding agents you already have on one Ubuntu 22.04 server. You reach it through Tailscale. It is alpha 0.2 and currently has a single user. It does not include a model. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
qiz029/dscode: A terminal coding agent for writing code on macOS 14 or glibc Linux, where sessions can hand work to each other. Windows is not supported. You bring your own model account. v0.7.54. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
assafkip/claudemy: A Claude Code skill that builds about twelve two-minute audio lessons on a topic you name, using the Claude account you already have. It needs Python 3 and ffmpeg. Natural voices need an ElevenLabs key. Without one, it uses the built-in macOS voices. v0.3.2. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3: Multilingual voice cloning that clones from a reference clip on your machine. Twenty-four languages include Cantonese, and there are twenty-one Chinese dialects. Tencent-Hunyuan/AuK: A 1.5B speech foundation model for generation and editing on your machine. It needs Python 3.10. The weights and the Qwen2.5-Omni encoder download separately. The code and weights are MIT. It is not a Cantonese specialist. This does not give you an install-free app.
LodyAI/Lody: A team workspace that dispatches coding agents you already have from desktop, phone, or the web. You sign in, and a machine connects with npx. It is not fully local yet. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
kharmanskyi/open-steps: A skill pack that makes the coding agent you already use report in plain language and give steps you can follow. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI. v0.4.8. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
pullboard-dev/pullboard: A board in your git repo that assigns work to agents you already have, and another agent has to verify a change before it merges. You start it with npx. v0.9.3. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
edenfunf/reelmimic: A style-matching video tool that makes a new video on your machine from a reference clip. It needs Claude Code or Codex that you already have, plus Node 22.18 and Python 3.10. It does not include a video model. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
ShenSeanChen/waku-agent: A local agent that runs a loop, memory, and evals on your machine. Memory is one SQLite file. You bring your own model key. A local dashboard is optional. v0.1.9. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
pgrundev/pgbot: A read-only Postgres checker that prints a health report for versions 14 through 18 on your machine. An agent can call it through MCP. It is beta, v0.9.0. Apache-2.0. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new agent.
coji/natural-japanese: A skill that rewrites workplace Japanese inside the coding agent you already use, and it does not add facts the source did not have. v1.6.4. MIT. This is Japanese, not Cantonese, and it does not give you a new model.
harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo: A short-video generator that turns a topic you give it into a script, voiceover, and finished clip. You bring your own LLM and media API keys, and it needs FFmpeg. You run it yourself. v1.3.9. MIT. It does not include a video model.
debpalash/VoiceStudio: A local voice studio for cloning and dubbing on your machine. Models download separately. The stable macOS build needs Apple silicon, and CPU inference is slower. v0.5.7. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a model without a download.
oil-oil/beautify-github-readme: A skill that designs a repository README inside Claude Code or Codex that you already have, so install steps and limits are easier to see. It does not include a model. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
alexgreensh/attention-span: A set of output styles that change how Claude Code talks to you, not how it writes code. There are three styles. You use the Claude account you already have. v0.12. AGPL-3.0. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new model.
MichaelKinsy/PiG: A Go port of the Pi coding agent that runs the model you already have in the terminal. The installed binary does not need Node. v0.5.3 is not stable yet, and Windows is a preview. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
CorentinJ/Real-Time-Voice-Cloning: A real-time voice-cloning toolbox that synthesizes English from a few seconds of reference audio. babysor/MockingBird: A Chinese voice-cloning toolbox that synthesizes Mandarin from a few seconds of reference audio. It needs Python 3.7 and a GPU, and the weights are separate.
