haidrrrry/claude-remotion-skill: A skill that makes motion-graphics videos with Remotion inside Claude that you already have. The result is re-renderable code, not a pixel video model. You install Remotion yourself. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
andyhuo520/vibe-knowledge: A Claude Code skill that turns one fact into a narrated short video inside Claude that you already have. Narration needs a MiMo key, and it also needs FFmpeg. The quality check uses macOS Vision. v1.0.0. MIT. This does not give you a video model.
egoist/waku: A native desktop that shows coding agents you already have on one machine. You install and sign in to at least one agent CLI first. v0.1.20. GPL-3.0. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new model.
Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill: A skill that makes the coding agent you already use review, fix, and check its work again. v2.1.0. MIT. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new model.
kyky2347/ALTA: A research trading desk where several agents check evidence and run a Shadow simulation on your machine. A real order needs a broker API you authorize. It is not investment advice, and it does not include a model. v0.25.0. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
DrewThomasson/ebook2audiobook: A converter that turns an e-book into an audiobook with chapters and voices on your machine. It can clone a voice, on CPU or GPU. The README says 1,158 languages, and Cantonese is not a dedicated target. v26.10.1. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model without a download.
jianchang512/pyvideotrans: A video translator that adds subtitles and dubbing to a video on your machine. You can pick a local model or an online API, and voice cloning needs a separate engine. It needs Python 3.10. v4.17. GPL-3.0. This does not give you a model with nothing to set up.
jaredrhod/fullstack-agent: A Claude Code installer that assembles memory, voice, and a face on your machine. It needs the Claude subscription you already have. It runs on Mac, Linux, and Windows. Webcam hands are optional. AGPL-3.0. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new model.
autonomous-ai/openharness: A native desktop that shows coding agents you already have, including agents on other machines. The app is for macOS and Linux. The relay only forwards ciphertext. v1.3.56. MIT. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new model.
agents-universe/agents-universe: A self-hosted company agent platform that runs ten ready-made roles in Docker. The model needs an API key you provide. Local setup skips sign-in by default, and a real deployment should turn that off. Apache-2.0. Python 3.12. This does not give you a new model.
nari-labs/dia: A 1.6B dialogue speech model that turns a script into English on a GPU. It can clone a 5 to 10 second reference clip. Weights download separately, and bfloat16 uses about 4.4 GB. Apache-2.0. English only, not Cantonese. This does not give you a model without a download.
Huanshere/VideoLingo: A video subtitle bench that transcribes, translates, aligns, and dubs on your machine. It needs your own model API key, and it also needs FFmpeg. Dubbing uses a separate engine. v3.1.1. Apache-2.0. Chinese is an input language, and Cantonese is not a dedicated target. This does not give you a video model.
context-labs/whip: A coding agent written in Go for long tasks on your machine. The desktop beta needs Apple Silicon and macOS 14. The CLI runs on macOS and Linux. The model needs a key you provide. v1.0.0. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
petergyang/human-review: A skill that lets you edit HTML and Markdown in the browser, then send the comments to the coding agent you already use. It stays on your machine, with no account and no API key. v0.8.2. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
pyang5166/gbro-collage-broll: A skill that turns about five seconds of voiceover into halftone paper-collage B-roll inside the agent you already use. You approve three gates first. The video needs a Gemini key and is billed by use. The default is 9:16 and silent. MIT. This does not give you a video model.
k2-fsa/OmniVoice: A zero-shot speech model for 600-plus languages that clones a voice on a GPU. Cantonese is on the language list. Weights download separately. It runs on NVIDIA or Intel Arc. v0.2.1. Apache-2.0. It is not one fixed Hong Kong voice. This does not give you a model without a download.
k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx: An offline speech toolkit for recognition, synthesis, and voice-activity detection on your machine. Models download separately. Some recognition models include Cantonese, and not every model does. It runs from Android through Linux. v2.0.1. Apache-2.0. It can run without the internet. This does not give you a preloaded model.
wquguru/shisei: A mannequin pose library for lining up a shot in the image tool you already use. It has 280 poses and five angles. The images are CC0 and the code is Apache-2.0. An adult series stays blurred until you open it. v0.4.1. It is not an image model. This does not give you a new model.
FengZhenfei/carrel: A self-hosted knowledge base that lets the agent you already use look up documents and images. The agent writes the answer. It needs Python 3.12 and Docker, and you connect the models. A search skill is included. v0.4.0. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
okf-memory/okf-agent-memory: A memory store written in Go so the coding agent you already use can keep project decisions. The notes stay in git, with no external database. It includes an MCP server. v0.7.2. MIT. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new model.
ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5: ACE-Step 1.5 is a local music model that turns text and lyrics into music on your machine. It is a different repository from the older ACE-Step. Weights download separately. A 6 GB GPU can try the 2B model. v0.1.8. MIT. Lyrics cover 50-plus languages, and Cantonese is not a dedicated target. This does not give you a model without a download.
QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS: A speech series for voice design and a 3-second clone on your machine. It has 0.6B and 1.7B sizes, and the weights download separately. Ten languages include Chinese and English, with Beijing and Sichuan voices, and Cantonese is not one of them. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model without a download.
Ryder-Sun/Meldwork: A local workspace that gathers agents you already have on an Apple silicon Mac. Writes need your permission. The preview build is not notarized. V1.0.9. Apache-2.0. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new model.
yc-duan/fastctx: An MCP tool that lets the agent you already use run and record work across your own machines. The desktop app covers Windows, macOS, and Linux, and there is also an Android app and a CLI. Data goes through your Hub. v0.2.6. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
abus-aikorea/voice-pro: A local voice interface that runs existing models for recognition, translation, and cloning. The README says Windows with an NVIDIA GPU is the verified setup, and Mac and Linux are not verified. Weights download separately, and Edge-TTS needs the internet. v4.0.0. GPL-3.0. Cantonese is not a dedicated target. This does not give you a model without a download.
PaddlePaddle/PaddleSpeech: A Paddle speech toolkit for recognition, synthesis, and translation on your machine. It includes a Cantonese synthesis example, and the rest of the toolkit is not Cantonese. Models are prepared separately. r1.5.0. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model with nothing to set up.
Station-Sciences/bot-crossing: A local view that turns coding-agent threads on your machine into little bots. It only reads harness files and does not write back to them. It needs Node 22.13. MIT. The author says it may not be maintained. This does not give you a new model.
MaxHu-xuan/task-state-guard: An embedded SQLite check that closes stuck agent tasks after a restart. It does not guess that an unknown result succeeded. You can preview the change before applying it. v0.1.0. Apache-2.0. It is not a queue. This does not give you a new model.
rany2/edge-tts: A Python module that calls Microsoft Edge's online voices from your program. It needs the internet, and you do not install Edge. Voices follow Microsoft's list, and this is not a Cantonese model. v7.3.1. Most of the code is LGPL-3.0. This does not give you a local model.
open-mmlab/Amphion: A research toolkit for speech, singing, and voice conversion on your machine. The code is MIT. The Emilia dataset is CC BY-NC, and weights are prepared separately. v0.1.1-alpha. Cantonese is not a dedicated target. This does not give you a model without a download.
notinferred/keypaste: A KeePass-compatible vault on your machine that gives an agent one field only after you allow it. The published piece is the v0.3.0 CLI, and the desktop app has no public release yet. The vault needs no account. Share links go through keypaste.com. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a new model.
sodiumsun/agenttrail: A local view of what the coding agents you already use are doing on your machine. Kitchen is an experimental preview and needs Node 20. It does not run the agents. MIT. It does not include a model. This does not give you a new model.
Paritok-official/paritok-4b-v1: A compression layer between the coding agent you already use and your model API. By default it runs a 4B model of about 2.5 GB on your machine, and that traffic stays local. Turning on their GPU server sends it out. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new model.
mozilla/TTS: An older Mozilla text-to-speech library for training and generating speech. The README says more than 20 languages, and the weights are separate. The last push was in November 2023. MPL-2.0. It is a different repository from Coqui TTS. Cantonese is not a dedicated target. This does not give you a model without a download.
espnet/espnet: An end-to-end speech toolkit for recognition, synthesis, and translation on PyTorch. Pretrained models can be downloaded, and training follows a recipe. Some recipes mention Cantonese, and it is not one ready-made Cantonese model. v202611. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model with nothing to set up.
Lightricks/LTX-2: The AlphaGen pipeline inside the official LTX-2.5 package. It generates one stage from a reference video and an IC-LoRA. The 22B weights download separately. A company with annual revenue of 10 million US dollars or more needs a separate commercial license. The license is the LTX-2.x Community License, which is not an OSI open-source license. This does not give you a model without a download.
PeterL1n/RobustVideoMatting: A human video-matting model that makes an alpha from a video without a green screen. It uses a recurrent network to remember time. The README says about 104 FPS of HD tensor throughput on a GTX 1080 Ti, and the conversion script is slower. MobileNetV3 and ResNet50 are both available. v1.0.0. GPL-3.0. It is not a general-object matte. This does not give you a model without a download.
PeterL1n/BackgroundMattingV2: High-resolution background matting that makes an alpha from a person video plus an empty-background photo you captured first. It needs that background photo, and it is not a green screen. The author later released RVM, and this is the older method. The README says about 60 FPS of HD tensor throughput on an RTX 2080 Ti, and the video conversion script is not real-time. Weights download separately. v1.0.0. MIT. This does not give you a model without a download.
0xpili/simplified-technical-english: An agent skill that tells the LLM you already have to write technical text in Simplified Technical English. The checker is Python 3 only. It cannot find every error, and it does not prove that the text meets the official specification. The word list comes from ASD-STE100 Issue 7 (2017), and that list is ASD's property. The skill text and scripts are MIT. It is not an official ASD document. This does not give you a model.
vshulcz/deja-vu: A local memory index that searches session history your coding agents already saved. The README lists 43 harnesses. Search stays on your machine and does not call an LLM by default. Semantic search sends the query to an embedding endpoint you configure. v0.23.5. MIT. It does not run the agents, and it does not give you a new model.
yetone/kill-ai-slop: An agent skill that scans a web project for common AI visual and copy habits and explains why each one reads as machine-made. The site catalogues 33 items in English, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. The scanner does not edit files. Apache-2.0. It is not a model. Only the coding agent you already have applies changes, and this does not give you a new interface.
voicepaw/so-vits-svc-fork: A singing-voice conversion fork for real-time timbre change on your machine. Models follow so-vits-svc 4.0, and 4.1 models are not supported. Install downloads pretrained weights automatically. The latest tag is v4.2.30. The license file starts with MIT and also includes the Apache-2.0 text. The README still says the project is no longer maintained. It does not turn text into speech, and it does not give you a model without a download.
netease-youdao/EmotiVoice: A multi-voice text-to-speech engine that reads English and Chinese from an emotion prompt. The README says more than 2000 voices. Weights download separately from ModelScope. The Docker path needs an NVIDIA GPU. Japanese and Korean are still unfinished. Apache-2.0. Cantonese is not included. This does not give you a model without a download.
Neywa-Labs/mlx-audio: An Apple Silicon toolbox that runs existing text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and speech-to-speech models on your Mac. It needs an M-series Mac. Models such as Kokoro, Qwen3-TTS, and Whisper download separately. Some models include Chinese, and Cantonese is not a dedicated target. v0.6.4. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
jaywalnut310/vits: The official code for the VITS paper. It turns text into speech in one stage. The paper's listening test uses the single-speaker English LJ Speech set, and there is also a multi-speaker VCTK training path. Pretrained weights are on Google Drive. The last push was in December 2023. MIT. It is not a finished product, and it is not Cantonese. This does not give you a model without a download.
addyosmani/agent-skills: Twenty-five engineering skills for the coding agent you already have. They cover the spec, the plan, the code, the tests, and the release. npx can install them into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and others. Installing one skill leaves out the shared checklists. 0.6.15. MIT. This is not a model, and it does not give you a new agent.
Leonxlnx/taste-skill: An agent skill that makes the coding agent you already have design websites and app screens instead of a generic landing page. It needs Node 22 and Chrome, Edge, or Chromium. Finding pictures needs the network, and the pictures come from the public domain or Creative Commons. One build takes about 30 to 45 minutes. v2.1.5. MIT. It does not need an API key, and it does not give you a model.
myshell-ai/MeloTTS: A multilingual text-to-speech library that reads English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean on your machine. The Chinese speaker can mix Chinese and English. The README says CPU inference is fast enough for real time. Weights are on Hugging Face. It has a web page and a CLI. The last push was in December 2024. MIT. Cantonese is not included. This does not give you a model without a download.
JuneYaooo/rea-video: An agent skill for Claude Code or Codex. It splits a video shot by shot and writes a plan to remake it. You need ffmpeg and Python 3.10. A model that can watch video, plus your own API key, makes the split and the prompts more precise. It still runs without that model. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
nexu-io/open-design: A local design workspace for making prototypes, pages, decks, and video with the AI agent you already have. Installers exist for macOS and Windows. Linux has to be built from source. Models use your own API key. Scrubbed safety telemetry stays on. v0.27.0. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
pbakaus/impeccable: A design-vocabulary skill that lets the coding agent you already have restyle a screen and catch AI-looking UI. The CLI can scan files without an agent. Scanning a web page needs Chrome or Edge. cli-v4.8.0. Apache-2.0. Generating a picture first is only available when your agent can make images. This does not give you a model.
espeak-ng/espeak-ng: A small text-to-speech program for Linux, Windows, and Android. It speaks more than a hundred languages and accents, including Cantonese. It uses formant synthesis, the voices ship inside the program, and the speech is less natural than recorded voices. The latest release is 1.52.0. GPL-3.0. It does not need a large downloaded model, and it does not give you a neural voice.
argmaxinc/argmax-oss-swift: A local Swift SDK that runs existing Whisper, Pyannote, and Qwen-TTS models on macOS 14. It needs Xcode 16. Android and live speaker labels are in a separate Pro SDK. v1.1.1. MIT. Weights download separately. This does not give you a new model.
OpenSparX/MasterAgent: A local C++ agent runtime. It runs fixed skills on your machine first, then calls a model you already have only when needed. The demo needs no model, network, or vehicle hardware. Qualcomm NPU support is not verified in this release. The open build is 0.4.0-alpha.3, and it is not the proprietary kernel. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything: An agent skill that turns a codebase into a searchable knowledge graph inside the coding agent you already have. Tree-sitter reads the structure, and the agent's model writes the explanations. The graph viewer needs only Node 18 and no API key. The latest release is v2.9.0. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
denizsafak/abogen: An audiobook tool that reads EPUBs, PDFs, and text on your machine and writes matching subtitles. It uses the existing Kokoro-82M model. Chinese means Mandarin and needs the extra misaki package. Mac needs espeak-ng. AMD GPUs are not supported on Windows. MIT. Cantonese is not included. This does not give you a new model.
cathrynlavery/diagram-design: An agent skill that draws 45 kinds of diagrams inside the coding agent you already have. Each diagram is one HTML file plus SVG. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others. It does not emit Mermaid. MIT. This does not give you a drawing model.
dograh-hq/dograh: A voice-agent platform you self-host with Docker on your machine for phone calls and conversation flows. It ships with their LLM, TTS, and STT, and you can switch in your own keys. Phone calls need a provider such as Twilio. dograh-v1.51.0. BSD-2-Clause. This does not give you a new speech model.
buxuku/SmartSub: A desktop subtitle tool for transcription, translation, dubbing, and burning subtitles on your machine. Transcription can use Whisper or FunASR, and the file does not have to be uploaded. The SenseVoice engine has a Cantonese option, and the whole app is not Cantonese. Dubbing uses existing models. v3.12.1. MIT. This does not give you a new model.
blader/humanizer: An agent skill that rewrites AI-sounding text inside the coding agent you already have, without changing what it says. It follows Wikipedia's signs of AI writing. The README says detectors still flag most of the output. v3.1.0. MIT. It is not a tool for passing detectors, and it does not give you a model.
ayghri/i-have-adhd: An agent skill that makes the coding agent you already have lead with the answer, number the steps, and drop the closing filler. The README says you do not need an ADHD diagnosis. v0.4.1. MIT. It is not a medical tool, and it does not give you a model.
liuzhao1225/YouDub-webui: A desktop app for localizing a video on your machine. It transcribes, translates, and clones the original voice sentence by sentence, then writes subtitles and a dubbed video. The language list is English, Chinese, and Japanese. It uses existing models that you install separately. v0.0.12. Apache-2.0. Cantonese is not included. This does not give you a new model.
remsky/Kokoro-FastAPI: An API wrapper around Kokoro-82M. It opens an OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech endpoint in Docker. Languages include English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, and Mandarin. NVIDIA has an image, and AMD is experimental. Apple Silicon runs directly and is not a container image. v0.9.2. Apache-2.0. Cantonese is not included. This does not give you a new model.
Generated-Computers/Locals: A local inference server for Apple Silicon Macs. It runs the coding agents you already have at the same time. The default model is Qwen3.5-4B, about 2.8 GB, and it runs one model at a time. A single request is about the same speed as mlx-lm. The README's 3x figure is for many requests at once. PyPI 0.2.2. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a new agent.
coreyhaines31/marketingskills: A set of marketing skills for the coding agent you already have. They cover conversion, copy, SEO, and analytics. Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor are supported. v2.14.0. MIT. It does not place ads by itself, and it does not give you a model.
ysharma3501/LuxTTS: A voice-cloning model that reads text on your machine from a reference recording. The README says one GPU can reach about 150 times real time, and it fits in 1 GB of video memory. Weights are on Hugging Face. CPU and Mac paths exist. Apache-2.0. The README does not list languages. This does not give you a model without a download.
K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills: A pack of scientific skills for the coding agent you already have. The README says 177 skills, covering biology, chemistry, medicine, and data analysis. Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and other hosts are supported. Some databases need you to apply for access. v2.72.0. MIT. It does not run lab experiments, and it does not give you a model.
VoltAgent/awesome-openclaw-skills: A list of OpenClaw skills you pick from ClawHub and use on your own machine. The README title says 5300+, the badge says 5200, and the GitHub description says 5400+, so the counts do not match. The list says the skills are not audited one by one. MIT. This repo does not contain the skill code, it does not run OpenClaw for you, and it does not give you a model.
MoonInTheRiver/DiffSinger: Official PyTorch code for singing-voice synthesis and text-to-speech. It runs on your machine from lyrics or text. The TTS docs use English LJSpeech, and the singing docs use PopCS and OpenCpop. The README specifies Python 3.8 and torch 1.9.0. Weights are on a 2022 GitHub release and download separately. MIT. The PopCS docs do not name a language. This is not Cantonese, and it does not give you a model without a download.
gradio-app/fastrtc: A Python library that turns your own function into a real-time audio or video stream over WebRTC or WebSockets. Voice-activity detection and text-to-speech are optional extras. The voice examples need your own API key. The phone helper needs a Hugging Face token. 0.0.34. MIT. It does not include a speech model, and it does not give you a model.
alibaba/open-code-review: A code-review CLI that writes line-level comments on your git diff. It needs Git 2.41 or newer, plus your own model endpoint and API key. Delegation mode can use the model of the coding agent you already have. v1.13.5. Apache-2.0. The README says its precision is higher than a general agent, but its recall is lower. This does not give you a model.
sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills: A pack of installable skills for the coding agent you already have. You use them to pick skills and preview a plan. The README says 2923+, while the GitHub description says 2884+, so the counts do not match. Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor are supported. v20.5.0. MIT. AAS Core does not rank skills for you. This does not give you a model.
OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano: A 0.1B multilingual text-to-speech model for real-time speech and reference-voice cloning on CPU, with 48 kHz stereo output. The README says 20 languages, but the table lists 19, including Chinese and English, and not Cantonese. Weights are on Hugging Face. The model card and the LICENSE file both say Apache-2.0. The README license section still says the license is unpublished. This does not give you a model without a download.
collabora/WhisperLive: A nearly live Whisper transcription server that runs an existing model on your machine. It supports faster-whisper, TensorRT, and OpenVINO. The model downloads separately. v0.10.0. MIT. This is not a new model, and it does not give you the weights.
reactive-resume/reactive-resume: A resume editor for writing and exporting a PDF in the browser. You can also self-host it. It includes 32 resume skills and an MCP server. Optional AI needs a provider you connect yourself. v6.1.0. MIT. This is not a general coding agent, and it does not give you a model.
wshobson/agents: A pack of coding-agent plugins that installs skills and subagents into the tool you already have. The README says 94 plugins, 185 skills, and 202 agents. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other hosts are supported. Two external plugins have their own licenses. MIT. There is no GitHub release. This does not give you a model.
OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS: A family of speech models for long-form speech, dialogue, and voice design on your machine. v1.5 is 8B. The README says 31 languages, including Cantonese. TTSD and Realtime follow their own model cards. Weights are on Hugging Face. The README says the llama.cpp low-memory mode can run the 8B model on an 8 GB GPU. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model without a download.
metavoiceio/metavoice-src: A 1.2B English text-to-speech model that clones American or British voices on your machine from about 30 seconds of reference audio. The README asks for at least 12 GB of GPU memory, Python 3.10 up to but not including 3.12, and torch 2.2.1. Arbitrary-length text is still unfinished. Weights are on Hugging Face. Apache-2.0. The last push was 2024-07. This is not Cantonese, and it does not give you a model without a download.
Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode: A multi-agent orchestration plugin for the Claude Code session you already have. It opens teams and skills there. It needs your own login or API key. The team CLI can open tmux workers. v5.7.30. MIT. This does not give you a model.
KoljaB/RealtimeTTS: A realtime text-to-speech library that connects existing engines on your machine. Qwen is the recommended engine, and the first run downloads its model. System voices and cloud engines are also included. Cloud engines need your own key. v0.8.10. MIT. This is not a new model, and it does not give you the weights.
0xShug0/audio.cpp: A pure C++ audio inference engine that runs existing models on your machine, with no Python. The README says 143 model families. Weights download separately and keep the original model license, and some of those licenses do not allow commercial use. NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, and CPU are supported. v0.9.4. The program is Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
ChatCut-Inc/agent-plugin: A video-editing plugin for the coding agent you already have. It changes your own footage, adds captions, and adds motion graphics. It needs a ChatCut account. Desktop is only macOS 13 or newer and Windows 10 or newer, so Linux cannot install Desktop. Remaking a video needs credit approval first. Apache-2.0. There is no release. It does not include the editor program, and it does not give you a model.
CuboiLeo/SuperMimic-Reproduced: An independent reproduction of a world model that tracks G1 motion in simulation. It is not official code, and it is not a real robot. LAFAN1 is CC BY-NC-ND, and the datasets are not included. The checkpoint is e8-boneseed-100k. It uses Python 3.12 and torch 2.14.1, and it was tried on an RTX 5090. Every flip still fails. MIT. This does not give you the datasets.
JCodesMore/ai-website-cloner-template: A website-rebuild skill for the coding agent you already have. It turns a site into a Next.js app. It needs Node.js 24 or newer. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode are supported. v0.6.1. MIT. The README says it must not be used for phishing or impersonation. This does not give you a model.
CopilotKit/CopilotKit: A frontend kit that adds chat and generative UI to the agent you already have. React, Angular, Vue, React Native, Slack, and Teams are supported. v1.84.1. MIT. CopilotKit Intelligence is a separate product. It does not include the agent, and it does not give you a model.
TensorSpeech/TensorFlowTTS: A TensorFlow 2 text-to-speech program that reads Chinese, Korean, English, French, and German on your machine. It recommends TensorFlow 2.6.0. The last release is v1.8 from 2021, and the last push was 2024-07. Weights are on Hugging Face. Apache-2.0. This is not Cantonese, and it does not give you a model without a download.
IAHispano/Applio: A voice-conversion tool that changes audio you have the rights to use, on your machine. The program and the weights in this repo are MIT, and the official unmodified build also has terms of use. 3.7.1. The README says later work is mainly security fixes. It has a Gradio interface. This is not a new foundation model, and it does not give you a new model.
ItzCrazyKns/Vane: A self-hosted AI answering engine that searches on your machine and cites sources. Docker bundles SearxNG. The model comes from Ollama or your own cloud key. The latest release is v1.12.2, and the last push was 2026-09. MIT. This does not give you a model.
can1357/oh-my-pi: A terminal coding agent that edits code on your machine. It needs your own model provider. The README says more than 60 providers. Bun is recommended, and the core includes Rust. v18.16.0. MIT. It does not include a model, and it does not give you one.
riffusion/riffusion-hobby: A realtime music program that turns text into sound on your machine. The code is MIT. The weights are CreativeML OpenRAIL-M, which is not OSI, and they download separately. Python 3.9 or 3.10. Realtime needs a fast GPU; the README names a 3090 or A10G. CPU is slow. The project says it is no longer maintained. The last release is v0.3.0. This does not give you a model without a download.
HeartMuLa/heartlib: A music model that writes a song on your machine from lyrics and tags. The README recommends the 3B checkpoint and HeartCodec. The 7B version is not released. Weights are on Hugging Face and download separately. A single GPU needs lazy load. The README says almost all languages, but it does not list them and does not name Cantonese. The code and weights are Apache-2.0. There is no release. This does not give you a model without a download.
agentscope-ai/QwenPaw: A personal AI assistant that chats on your machine or in the cloud. Local models download in the interface and do not need an API key. It can also use Ollama or a cloud provider. Python 3.11 up to but not including 3.14. The latest release is v2.3.0-beta.2, and it is still a beta. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model without a download.
virgiliojr94/book-to-skill: A skill for the coding agent you already have. It turns a document you have the rights to use into a skill. PDF, EPUB, DOCX, and other formats are supported. rsxdalv/TTS-WebUI: A multi-model voice interface that runs existing text-to-speech and music models on your machine. Extensions are not installed by default. gcui-art/suno-api: An unofficial client that asks suno.ai to make music from your machine. Suno itself is not open source, and it has no official API. VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills: A skill catalog for finding links to existing skills in the coding agent you already have. Each skill keeps its author's license, and some upstream projects may not be open source. There is no release. This does not give you a model.
esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix: An open-source coding assistant that reads and edits a project and runs commands on your machine. You choose and pay for the model. lucidrains/musiclm-pytorch: An unofficial PyTorch reimplementation for building MusicLM in a research setting. You train it yourself. The last release is 0.2.8, and the last push stopped in 2023-09. MIT. This does not give you a trained model.
elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python: The official Python SDK for calling ElevenLabs cloud voices from your program. The service itself is not open source. You need your own API key, and the models stay on their machines. Python 3.8 or newer. The latest release is v2.76.0. The SDK is MIT. This does not give you a local model.
andrew-babo/muse4ai: A local Windows bridge that hands your signed-in Muse session to a coding agent on your machine. The badge says v2.0.0-beta.32, and there is no release. MIT. This does not give you Muse or a model.
Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios: A Claude Code skill pack that turns one session of the Claude Code you already have into a game-studio workflow. The README badge says 49 agents and 74 skills, while the GitHub description says 72 skills. You need your own Claude Code, Python 3, and Bash. v1.2.0. MIT. It does not include a game, and it does not give you a model.
pnnbao97/VieNeu-TTS: An on-device text-to-speech model for Vietnamese and English that clones a voice on your machine. The default is v3 Turbo at 48 kHz. The full v3 model is not out yet. Weights are on Hugging Face. The code and the weights are Apache-2.0. It is not Cantonese. The latest GitHub release is app-v0.18.22. There is no macOS installer yet. This does not give you the weights without a download.
AutoArk/GPA: A speech model for speech recognition and text to speech. mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: A skill pack for security work in the coding agent you already have. It is not an official Anthropic product. The description says 817 skills, and the badge says 818. You need your own agent. v1.3.0, and the last push was 2026-08. Apache-2.0. The README says to test only systems you are allowed to test. This does not give you a model.
enhuiz/vall-e: An unofficial PyTorch reimplementation for building VALL-E in a research setting. You train it yourself, and there is no pretrained checkpoint. It was only tested on Python 3.10.7. KevinWang676/Bark-Voice-Cloning: A voice-cloning interface that runs Bark and other existing models on your machine. It is not a new model. Bark is weak at Chinese, and Chinese cloning uses Sambert instead. It is not Cantonese. Weights download on first run, and each model keeps its own license. Python 3.10 or newer. There is no release, and the last push was 2026-05. The interface is MIT. This does not give you the weights without a download.
iOfficeAI/AionUi: A desktop app that uses its built-in agent and the CLI agents you already have, on your machine. This does not give you a model.
vxcontrol/pentagi: A self-hosted multi-agent system for penetration testing on systems you are allowed to test. You choose the model, which can be a cloud provider or Ollama. The work runs inside an isolated Docker sandbox. v2.2.0, and the last push was 2026-10. MIT. This does not give you a model.
readbeyond/aeneas: A forced-alignment tool that lines up a recording with text. It is not a speech-synthesis model. It uses eSpeak by default, and you also install FFmpeg. The README confirms 38 languages, and the list does not include Chinese or Cantonese. The latest release is v1.7.3 from 2017, and the last push was 2026-07. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a speech model.
PlayVoice/whisper-vits-svc: A singing-voice conversion engine that turns a sung voice into another timbre on your machine. It does not turn text into speech, and it does not work in real time. This does not give you the weights without a download.
davila7/claude-code-templates: A component catalog and CLI for installing skills and agents into the Claude Code you already have. It is not an official Anthropic product. The README says about 1,900 components, and the skills column says 890+. The latest release is v1.29.7, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
topoteretes/cognee: An agent memory library that turns documents into a searchable knowledge graph on your machine. With no API key it uses a small local model, but that model downloads on first use. Generating an answer needs a separate LLM. Python 3.10 through 3.14. The latest release is v1.6.6, and there were later pushes through 2026-11. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model without a download.
Camb-ai/MARS5-TTS: An English text-to-speech model that clones a reference voice on your machine. The open release is English only. The 140-plus languages belong to the closed product. This does not give you the weights without a download.
CloakHQ/CloakBrowser: A Playwright replacement wrapper that launches a Chromium build the README says can pass bot-detection tests. That result is a claim, not a guarantee. The wrapper is MIT. The browser binary is CloakHQ's proprietary build, and the latest major version requires a paid subscription. The latest release tag includes pro. This is not a model, and it does not give you an open-source browser binary.
feder-cr/Jobs_Applier_AI_Agent: A job agent that searches and submits applications on your machine from a resume you already have. You need your own OrcaRouter key. Automatic applications may not fit a site's terms. The latest release tag is jobs-20261105-080345. MIT. It does not include the jobs, and it does not give you a model.
riffusion/riffusion-app-hobby: A real-time music web app that connects to an inference server you run separately. This does not give you a model.
googleworkspace/cli: The Workspace command line that calls Drive, Gmail, and Calendar on your machine. You need your own Google account. The opening says 40+ skills, and the skills section says 100+. The latest release is v0.22.5 from 2026-03, and there were later pushes through 2026-11. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
decolua/9router: A local router that connects a coding agent you already have to other model providers on your machine. MIT. This does not give you a model.
pndurette/gTTS: An unofficial client that asks Google Translate to speak from your program. It is not Google Cloud text-to-speech, and it is not a local model. This does not give you a model.
trycua/cua: A computer-use tool that lets an agent you already have use sandboxes and desktops on your machine. The SDK, Driver, and Lume are MIT. The latest release is v0.12.1 from 2026-11.
nanocoai/nanoclaw: A messaging assistant that runs an agent you already have inside a container, then connects channels such as Telegram. The latest release is v2026.10.1-rc.2. MIT. This does not give you a model.
marytts/marytts: Java text-to-speech that starts a server on your machine. Language modules include English, German, French, Italian, Russian, and others, and there is no Cantonese. This is not a cloud service, and it does not give you a new model.
Sandflow-ai/sand3d: A Python library for writing programs that build 3D on Blender's bpy. It is for an LLM you already have. Python is only 3.11 or 3.13, and bpy is 4.5 or 5.2. ComposioHQ/composio: An SDK that connects an agent you already have to app tools. The README says 1000+ tools, and that is a claim. You need your own API key, and the tools run on their cloud. jackwener/OpenCLI: A command line that lets an agent operate websites in Chrome where you are already signed in. You need your own account, and each site's terms still apply. nateshmbhat/pyttsx3: An offline Python library that calls the system voices already on your machine. Windows uses SAPI5, macOS uses the system voice, and Linux needs eSpeak. digitalsamba/claude-code-video-toolkit: A Claude Code skill pack for writing a script, adding a voice, and rendering a video on your machine. This does not give you a model.
TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory: A team memory server that turns conversations, documents, and code into reusable memory on your machine. You need your own LLM, and Node 22.16 or newer. This does not give you a model.
Infisical/infisical: A secrets and certificate platform for keys, certificates, and agent access on your machine, or on their cloud. Enterprise features in the ee directories need a separate license. ddalcu/mlx-serve: A local model server that runs models you download on Apple Silicon, with a Linux build for NVIDIA. The Mac app needs macOS 26.2. Chat, images, video, music, and speech are all features. The latest release is v26.11.2. MIT. This does not give you a model.
jik876/hifi-gan: A vocoder that turns a mel spectrogram into a waveform on your computer. It is not a complete text-to-speech system. This does not give you a ready voice.
patch-gg/trompe: A browser tool that projects textures onto a gray level and exports glTF. Planning and baking run on your machine's GPU. The image models run on fal, and you need your own key. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
amap-cvlab/ABot-Recon: Streaming 3D reconstruction that estimates a point cloud and a relative pose for frames of your video. It uses only the latest 12 frames and does not keep long-range memory. This does not give you a commercial license.
DIYgod/pinky: A phone gateway that lets an agent you already have operate an iPhone or Android from your machine. Risky steps wait for your approval. It is pre-alpha. You need your own phone and agent. The latest release is v2026.1109.17. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
sarpstar/cinecode: A video skill that asks Claude Code or Cursor to build a film in code on your machine. It needs Node 22, Python 3.9, ffmpeg, and Chrome. janestreet/agent_skills: A Jane Street skill pack. It currently has only socratic-tutor, which asks an agent you already have to teach with one question at a time on your machine. You need your own model. There is no GitHub release. MIT. This does not give you a model.
zeekk0/OpenAmika: A Live2D companion that talks with you and remembers you on Windows. The code is MIT. The voice and Live2D model are under a personal-use license, which is not OSI. win4r/video-director: A Claude Code skill that builds a short film in code on your computer and then checks it. The README recommends Opus 5.5, and other agents can follow it too. It needs ffmpeg and Python. There is no GitHub release. MIT. This does not give you a model.
artcraft-android/procraft: A painting app for drawing on your Android tablet, Windows, and Linux, with pressure brushes, layers, and 3D painting. It is in beta. It needs Android 10 or newer. The latest release is v0.0.5-beta. MIT or Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
alexturkey/voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi: Local voice design that describes a voice and reads it on an NVIDIA card. Ready-made voices include Turkish and Mandarin, and there is no Cantonese. alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion: An art-animation skill that asks a coding agent you already have to draw moving pictures in code on your machine. It needs uv, ffmpeg, and Playwright Chromium. cutetailbud/ff-ruyijs: A headless Firefox engine that lets an agent you already have run a site's JavaScript on your machine. It needs Python 3.10. Closed-source use needs a separate commercial license. The latest release is v0.3.6. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a model.
ppmpreetham/BUI: A Blender interface library for drawing a Blender-style interface inside your own program. It does not include Blender itself. It has no accessibility support. On macOS it draws on the CPU only. The latest release is v0.5.0. GPL-3.0-or-later. This does not give you a model.
qianshuixia/shrimpreel: A paid video-site template for selling a one-photo-to-video service on Cloudflare. This does not give you a video model.
vladimirrott/mojo-dllm: Local inference for diffusion language models, for running LLaDA and Dream on Linux x86-64. It needs Mojo 1.1, AVX2, and about 6 GB of memory. AhmadHassan-BTed/B: A desktop companion that watches your own screen and talks with you on your Windows machine. Linux and macOS are experimental. OpenMontageInc/OpenMontage: An open-source agent video production system that produces video with multiple production pipelines and tools. phone-harness/mcp: An MCP connector that lets an agent you already have drive a cloud iPhone or Android emulator, and the docs also cover running it yourself. The cloud phones are paid. You have to sign in. There is no GitHub release. MIT. This does not give you a phone or a model.
Rayhane-mamah/Tacotron-2: An unofficial TensorFlow implementation for training Tacotron-2 on your machine. Preprocessing only supports LJSpeech-style English data. JosssphZhou/poki: A local iPhone agent that lets an agent you already have operate your iPhone from a Mac or Windows machine. It needs iOS 18, USB, an Apple Account, and a loopback proxy. opensec-git/Pi-Bolt: A native build of the Pi coding agent for Linux, macOS, Windows, or Android Termux. It does not need Node. The speed figures are a comparison against Pi 1.4.0. You need your own model. The latest release is bolt-v1.1.7. MIT. This does not give you a model.
lifeiteng/vall-e: An unofficial PyTorch implementation for training VALL-E on one GPU. The examples are English and Mandarin, and Cantonese is not described. DigitalPhonetics/IMS-Toucan: A multilingual text-to-speech toolkit for training or inference on your machine. The language list includes Cantonese, and the quality was not checked here. wangzhishou/OneBox: An Android agent toolbox that asks a model you already have to drive the tools inside the app on your phone. The cloud path needs your own key. fatchord/WaveRNN: A PyTorch vocoder and text-to-speech system for reading English on your machine. The README says it needs Python 3.6 or newer and PyTorch 1 with CUDA. travisvn/openai-edge-tts: A local API that sends text to Microsoft Edge's online read-aloud from your machine, with an interface that imitates OpenAI. It needs the network. alchaincyf/nuwa-skill: A skill that asks an agent you already have to research a public name on your machine and write that thinking style down. This does not give you a model.
kestra-io/kestra: An open-source orchestrator for arranging workflows in YAML on your machine, including AI steps. Enterprise features are not in this Apache program. It needs Docker. The latest release is v2.0.9, and there were later pushes. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
fikrikarim/parlor: A research preview for on-device speech and camera input on a Mac with Apple silicon or on Linux with a GPU. It needs Python 3.12 and llama.cpp. Models download on the first run. salu133445/musegan: Multi-track music generation for building short phrases of bass, drums, guitar, piano, and strings on your machine. The data is the Lakh Pianoroll set. Vibha-Ramprakash/claude-video-effects: A video skill that adds effects to your talking-head clip inside Claude Code. It needs ffmpeg and Python. The full studio is not in this repository. There is no GitHub release. MIT. This does not give you a model.
chroma-core/chroma: A vector search database for storing and searching embeddings on your machine. You need your own data and embedding model. The cloud version is paid. techjarves/Portable-Local-Studio: A local studio for images, GGUF chat, Whisper, and Kokoro on Windows, Linux, or macOS. alibaba/page-agent: An in-page GUI agent that controls your own web page from text. You need your own language model. It does not use screenshots. Crossing pages needs a separate extension. The latest release is v1.12.4, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
alirezarezvani/claude-skills: A skill pack that asks an agent you already have, in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others, to do engineering and marketing work. The README says there are 411 skills. You need your own model. The latest release is v2.14.9. MIT. This does not give you a model.
High-Logic/Genie-TTS: An ONNX inference engine for running GPT-SoVITS V2 or V2ProPlus on a CPU. It needs Python 3.10. The first run downloads about 391 MB of resources. QwenLM/qwen-code: A coding agent in the terminal and editor for changing code in your own project. It needs Node 22, or the project's installer. alchaincyf/huashu-design: A design skill that, in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others, turns one sentence into a web page, an app prototype, an editable deck, and an infographic. HiThink-Tech/Financial-API: An official Tonghuashun client for A-share market data, used through an API, MCP, a CLI, or Python to look up quotes, financial statements, and indexes. software-mansion/react-native-executorch: A React Native on-phone inference library for running exported models, including vision, language models, reading text aloud, and speech-to-text. feiskyer/claude-code-settings: A Claude Code skill pack for switching among research, GitHub work, and images. Image generation is only two of the skills, gpt-image and nanobanana. igorls/comfyui-h3-editor: An H3 timeline editor inside ComfyUI that, on your own GPU, writes shots, renders them, and cuts the film. The pack does not download weights. You need ComfyUI 0.43 or newer. It also includes an agent skill. The latest release is v0.2.0. GPL-3.0. This does not give you a model.
dsauce/stickman-kino: A stickman video skill that, in a coding agent, writes the scenes and then draws every frame in code on your machine. There is no video model. Speech uses local Kokoro, and the music is generated by code. You need Node 18. The latest release is v1.0.0, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a video model.
PUSHINGSQUARES/pushing-creation: A cinematic prompt skill that, in Claude Code, writes style packs and storyboards. Rendering needs your own provider keys in Keychain. Without a key it only writes markdown. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-05-12. MIT. This does not give you a model.
magichourhq/skills: A Magic Hour skill pack that, in Codex and Claude Code, does image-to-video, face swap, and image generation. You need your own account and credits. The skills are free to install. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-11-01. MIT. This does not give you a model.
pixelab-ch/higgsfield-skills: Fifteen Higgsfield skills that, in Claude, write image and video prompts. Prompt writing works without the MCP. Generation needs your own Higgsfield account and credits. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-05-25. MIT. This does not give you a model.
Jakedismo/visual-explainer-extension: A Gemini CLI extension that turns terminal output into HTML diagrams and generates images with Gemini. You need your own Gemini access. It is not a general image model. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-03-05. MIT. This does not give you a model.
expo/exact: A cross-platform UI framework that runs one app on the web, macOS, iOS, and Linux. A coding agent can build, run, and test it on your machine. You need Xcode, Rust, Bun, and Chrome. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-11-11. MIT. It is not an image tool and does not give you a model.
Fosowl/agenticSeek: A local agent that browses and writes programs on your machine. You need Python 3.10, Docker, and your own Ollama model, such as Deepseek 14B. A cloud key is optional. Voice is not finished. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-10-22. GPL-3.0. This does not give you a model.
ningzimu/codex-ppt-skill: A PPT skill that, in Codex, turns a document into a picture for each slide and assembles a pptx locally. The pages are images, so you cannot edit the words directly. It uses Codex built-in image generation or your own API key. The latest release is v0.6.0, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
ThioJoe/Auto-Synced-Translated-Dubs: A subtitle dubbing tool that, on your machine, redubs a video to another language using the subtitle timings. You need your own Google or DeepL translation key, and an Azure or Google voice key. Python 3.9 and FFmpeg. The latest release is v0.21.0, and there were later pushes. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a voice model.
Fagan1024/smart-video-editor: A skill that watches footage before it cuts. In Claude Code it extracts frames, asks the agent's own vision model to score them, and renders with FFmpeg. Fonts and background music are not in the repository. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-07-26. MIT. This does not give you a video model.
yikart/AiToEarn: A content agent that, in Claude Code, calls Grok, Veo, Seedance, and Nano Banana to make video and images, then posts them to social platforms. You need your own AiToEarn key and accounts. Node 20.18. The latest release is v2.5.0, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
agentskills/agentskills: The Agent Skills specification and its docs, so different agents can share one SKILL.md format. This repository is the standard. It is not a skill pack, and it does not include a model. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-11-04. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
liustack/modlens: A vision plugin for text-only models that, in DeepSeek and GLM, reads an image you paste and returns OCR and layout JSON. You need your own Gemini key or another key. It does not generate images. The latest release is v3.27.3, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a vision model.
sgl-project/sglang-omni: A serving runtime for speech and multimodal models that runs existing ASR and TTS on your machine or a GPU. You download the weights yourself. The latest GitHub release is Voxt v2.0.3, and there were later pushes. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
webadderallorg/Recordly: A desktop app for screen recording and editing that makes demo videos on macOS 14, Windows 10, and Linux. It adds automatic zooms and cursor polish. It is not a generative model. The latest release is v1.4.0, and there were later pushes. AGPL-3.0. This does not give you a video model.
titanwings/distilly: A person-profile skill that, in Claude Code, turns messages and documents you provide into a Person Profile. It does not copy the person. Python 3.9. The latest release is v0.01, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
dapr/dapr: A distributed runtime that runs applications and agent workflows in the cloud and at the edge. It is not a video tool, and it does not include a model. The latest release is v1.19.1, and there were later pushes. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
kangarooking/cangjie-skill: A distillation skill that, in Claude Code, turns books, subtitles, and podcast text into a callable skill. It does not download or generate video. Python 3.10. The latest release is v2.5.0, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
earthtojake/text-to-cad: A CAD skill pack that, in an agent, writes parts and assemblies in Python and exports STEP, GLB, and STL. It uses OpenCASCADE, not a neural network. Blender renders need your own GPU. It sends usage statistics by default. The latest release is v0.11.8, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
browserbase/stagehand: An SDK for browser agents that opens a browser on your machine to extract data and operate web pages. You need your own model API key. The latest GitHub release is stagehand-server v3.7.7, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
dexhunter/seedance2-skill: A Seedance 2.0 prompt skill that, in Claude Code and Cursor, writes camera and ad prompts. It does not call the model, and it does not render a video. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-09-19. MIT. This does not give you a model.
HybridRobotics/supermimic: A differentiable world model for whole-body humanoid motion that trains a tracking policy on a GPU. You also clone the research mjlab repository. It does not include trained weights. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-11-11. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
activepieces/activepieces: A workflow platform that connects AI agents and MCP servers on your machine. The community code is MIT. The packages/ee directory is a separate paid license, not MIT. You need your own model key. The latest release is 0.93.0, and there were later pushes. This does not give you a model.
pascalorg/editor: A building editor in the browser that, through local MCP, lets an agent edit building models. Local mode needs no account. The hosted workspace needs a sign-in. It is not a generative model. The latest release is CLI 1.1.0, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a model.
Agentchengfeng/chengfeng-videocut-skills: A video-editing skill plugin that, in Codex, asks a workbench to cut talking-head footage and captions. This repository does not include the editor. The public runtime is still v0.4.11, while the new workbench needs 0.5.9, so the new commands stop. Node 18. The latest release is v0.10.11, and there were later pushes. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
SharpAI/DeepCamera: A local camera skill platform that analyzes video from cameras you connect yourself. You download Qwen or another model yourself. It does not generate video. The latest release is v2026.3, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not ship the weights with the install.
nexu-io/openmotion: An agent that builds a video in HTML, remakes a reference on your machine, and renders an MP4. Images, extra shots, and music need your own keys. Node 22.18. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-11-11. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
NVIDIA/SkillSpector: A security scanner for agent skills that checks for injection and exfiltration before you install. The static scan does not need a model. The semantic check needs your own key. Python 3.12. The latest release is v2.13.4, and there were later pushes. Apache-2.0. This does not give you a model.
ModelTC/LightX2V: An inference framework for images and video that runs existing text-to-video and image-to-video models on your GPU. You download the weights yourself from Hugging Face. The latest release is 0.6.1, and there were later pushes. Apache-2.0. This does not ship a model with the install.
Agents365-ai/video-podcast-maker: A skill that turns a topic into a 4K video. In an agent it renders with Remotion. Edge speech needs no key. AI assets need your own keys. Python 3.8, Node 18, and FFmpeg. The latest GitHub release is v5.2.1, and there were later pushes. The README says v5.3.0. MIT. This does not give you a model.
threerocks/article2media: A skill that turns an article into cards and a narrated short video in Claude Code and Codex. Speech uses local VoxCPM2, and captions use Whisper. You need Node 22 and Chrome. The latest release is v2.2.0, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a video model.
weibo-job/guagua-animation-skills: Nine silent-animation skills that, in Codex, write characters, storyboards, and prompts. The repository says the end-to-end media run is not finished. Images and video need your own tools and may cost money. Without those tools it only writes text. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-11-04. MIT. This does not give you a model.
lhlGitHub/threejs-architecture-effects: A Three.js architecture skill that, in Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor, builds a rotatable 3D building. It is generated by code. It needs no API key, and it is not a video model. You need Node. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-09-22. MIT. This does not give you a model.
mkiol/dsnote: An offline Linux notes app that does speech to text, reading aloud, and translation on your machine. The install package does not include the models. You download them inside the app. The latest release is b4.9.1-1, and there were later pushes. MPL-2.0. This does not ship the weights with the install.
met4citizen/TalkingHead: A 3D lip-sync class in the browser that moves an avatar with speech in Three.js. You need your own model and a TTS key. It does not generate video. The latest release is v1.8.2, and there were later pushes. MIT. This does not give you a voice model.
waybarrios/vllm-mlx: An Apple Silicon inference server that, on a Mac, runs text, image, video, and speech models you download yourself. Python 3.10. The latest release is v0.6.0, and there were later pushes. Apache-2.0. This does not ship the weights with the install.
flohoeller/affectui: affectUI is a React 19 component library for showing an agent's tool calls and approvals in your app. Pro items are not in this repo. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-11-10. MIT. It does not run an agent and only gives you the interface.
slopus/happy: This repo is the mobile app, the original CLI, and the relay. It runs Claude, Codex, and Grok on your machine with subscriptions you already pay for. The GitHub release is CLI v1.2.5, while the package says 1.2.6, and there were later pushes. MIT. It is not a skill and does not give you a model.
kan-bayashi/ParallelWaveGAN: An unofficial PyTorch vocoder that turns a mel spectrogram into a waveform, including HiFi-GAN. Download the weights separately and check the dataset license yourself. GitHub release v0.6.1 matches PyPI, and there were later pushes. Python 3.8. MIT. It does not speak from text and does not give you a full speech model.
NVIDIA/NemoClaw: NemoClaw is an Apache-2.0 sandbox that runs OpenClaw, Hermes, or Deep Agents inside OpenShell. You need a DGX or WSL host, and you choose the inference provider. Node 22.19. There is no GitHub release, and the latest push was on 2026-11-12. It is alpha. This does not give you a model.
ekwek1/soprano: Soprano is a local text-to-speech model that turns text into 32 kHz speech on a CPU or GPU. The 80M weights are not in the repo. Download them from Hugging Face. Python 3.10. There is no GitHub release, the package says 0.2.0, and the latest push was on 2026-01-16. Apache-2.0. This does not ship the weights with the install.
MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-MCP: The official MiniMax MCP server that, in Claude or Cursor, calls the cloud for speech, images, and video. You need your own API key, and use can cost money. Python 3.10. There is no GitHub release, the package says 0.0.19, and the latest push was on 2026-11-10. MIT. It does not run the models on your machine and does not give you the weights.
